```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import tables as T          # complex tables: merged cells, footnotes (T.<builder>(...).show())
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat
import re
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DOC = "PCR-010"
UO = "ufdf"
UO_TITLE = "Ultrafiltration / Diafiltration (Step 10)"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ formatting
def mn(s):
    """A formatted number with a true minus sign, and no sign on a value that rounds to zero."""
    s = str(s)
    if s.startswith("-"):
        return ("−" + s[1:]) if any(ch in "123456789" for ch in s) else s[1:]
    return s

def fx(x, d=2):
    return mn(f"{float(x):,.{d}f}")

def fg(x):
    return mn(f"{float(x):g}")

def pv(p):
    return "< 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"{p:.3f}"

def pe(p):
    return "p < 0.001" if p < 0.001 else f"p = {p:.3f}"

WORDS = {1: "one", 2: "two", 3: "three", 4: "four", 5: "five", 6: "six", 7: "seven",
         8: "eight", 9: "nine", 10: "ten", 11: "eleven", 12: "twelve"}

def w(n):
    return WORDS.get(int(n), f"{int(n)}")

def Cap(s):
    return s[:1].upper() + s[1:]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ parameters (config)
uo = CFG.unit_op(UO)
STEP_N = uo.step
PK = [p.key for p in uo.parameters]
assert PK == ["diavolumes", "tmp", "final_conc"]
PRM = {k: uo.param(k) for k in PK}
NAME = {k: PRM[k].name for k in PK}                          # as the config names it
nm = {k: NAME[k][0].lower() + NAME[k][1:] for k in PK}       # inside a sentence
UNIT = {k: PRM[k].unit for k in PK}
SP = {k: float(PRM[k].setpoint) for k in PK}
NOR = {k: tuple(map(float, PRM[k].nor)) for k in PK}
RNG = {k: tuple(map(float, PRM[k].prange)) for k in PK}
CLS = {k: PRM[k].classification for k in PK}
N_P = len(PK)
for k in PK:
    # the NOR and set-point in force are those the studies were planned against
    assert tuple(map(float, PRM[k].nor_characterized)) == NOR[k]
    assert PRM[k].setpoint_characterized is None or float(PRM[k].setpoint_characterized) == SP[k]
    assert RNG[k][0] <= NOR[k][0] <= SP[k] <= NOR[k][1] <= RNG[k][1]
assert set(CLS.values()) == {"KPP"}                         # every parameter of the step is a KPP
EXT_LOW = {k: RNG[k][0] < NOR[k][0] for k in PK}
EXT_HIGH = {k: RNG[k][1] > NOR[k][1] for k in PK}
assert EXT_LOW == {"diavolumes": False, "tmp": False, "final_conc": True} and all(EXT_HIGH.values())

def u_(k, v):
    return f"{fg(v)} {UNIT[k]}"

def rng_s(k):
    return f"{fg(RNG[k][0])}–{fg(RNG[k][1])} {UNIT[k]}"

# the number of diavolumes is counted to its target and never run below its minimum, so its NOR is
# one-sided (owner, 2026-10-11): at least NOR low. NOR high is kept for the simulation spread only.
ONE_SIDED = {k: getattr(PRM[k], "nor_one_sided", None) for k in PK}
assert ONE_SIDED == {"diavolumes": "low", "tmp": None, "final_conc": None}

def nor_cell(k):
    return f"≥ {fg(NOR[k][0])}" if ONE_SIDED[k] == "low" else f"{fg(NOR[k][0])}–{fg(NOR[k][1])}"

def nor_s(k):
    return f"{nor_cell(k)} {UNIT[k]}"

def sp_s(k):
    return u_(k, SP[k])

DS_TARGET = float(CFG.raw()["meta"]["drug_substance_target_g_per_l"])
assert DS_TARGET == SP["final_conc"]
SCALE_L = f"{int(V['commercial_scale_l']):,}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ studies, equipment, registers
CHR = csv("study_chronology.csv")
CHR = CHR[CHR["step"] == UO].set_index("id")
SDM_ID, UNI_ID, UNI2_ID = "S-UFDF-SDM", "S-UFDF-UNI", "S-UFDF-UNI2"
assert set(CHR.index) == {SDM_ID, UNI_ID, UNI2_ID}
SDM_START, SDM_END, SDM_EQ = CHR.loc[SDM_ID, ["start", "end", "equipment"]]
UNI_START, UNI_END, UNI_EQ = CHR.loc[UNI_ID, ["start", "end", "equipment"]]
UNI2_START, UNI2_END, UNI2_EQ = CHR.loc[UNI2_ID, ["start", "end", "equipment"]]
EQT = equipment_df().set_index("Equipment")
CALDUE = {e: EQT.loc[e, "Next calibration due"] for e in {SDM_EQ, UNI_EQ, UNI2_EQ}}
assert all(EQT.loc[e, "Calibration status"] == "in calibration at execution" for e in CALDUE)
assert SDM_EQ == UNI_EQ != UNI2_EQ
assert SDM_END < UNI_START                     # the offset runs were complete before characterization
for _s in CHR.index:
    assert CHR.loc[_s, "end"] < CALDUE[CHR.loc[_s, "equipment"]]
assert UNI2_START > INV["closed"] and UNI2_END < EFFECTIVE_DATE and UNI_END < REV1["effective"]

PDS = PLAN_DISCREPANCIES[DOC]
PD = {int(_p["id"].rsplit("-", 1)[1]): _p["id"] for _p in PDS}
assert list(PD) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] and all(_p["plan"] == "PCP-010" for _p in PDS)
assert PDS[0]["studies"] == [UNI2_ID] and all(_p["studies"] == [] for _p in PDS[1:])
assert UNI2_EQ in PDS[0]["done"] and SDM_EQ in PDS[0]["done"]          # PD-010-01 names the second skid
assert "conductivity" in PDS[1]["subject"].lower() and "minimum" in PDS[6]["subject"].lower()
assert "lowers the residual process buffer further" in PDS[6]["reason"] and "only lowers" not in PDS[6]["reason"]
assert PDS[7]["subject"].startswith("Aggregate verified") and "§7.2" in PDS[7]["planned"] and "§7.5" in PDS[7]["done"]
N_PD = len(PDS)
PD1 = PD[1]
EVS = dev_facts(DOC)
assert list(EVS["dev_id"]) == ["DEV-010-01", "DEV-010-02"] and (EVS["disposition"] == "retained").all()
EV1_EQ = EVS.loc[0, "equipment"]
EV2_METHOD = EVS.loc[1, "method"]
assert EV1_EQ == SDM_EQ and pd.isna(EVS.loc[1, "equipment"]) and EV2_METHOD == "AMV-3019"
assert NOR["tmp"][1] < dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi <= RNG["tmp"][1]
assert not ({"study", "run"} & set(EVS.columns))      # the event record names no study and no run
_cex = D.iac_limit("cex", "aggregate_out_pct")
assert _cex[2] == "upper" and "tightened on verification" in D.acceptance_basis("cex", "aggregate_out_pct")
CEX_AG = float(_cex[1])
assert NOR["final_conc"][0] <= dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l < SP["final_conc"]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the univariate study
UNIALL = csv("univariate_studies.csv")
assert set(UNIALL.loc[UNIALL["step"] == UO, "study"]) == {UNI2_ID}   # S-UFDF-UNI has no recorded result
U = UNIALL[UNIALL["study"] == UNI2_ID].copy().reset_index(drop=True)
LEVELS = ["low", "low-mid", "set-point", "mid-high", "high"]
assert set(U["level"]) == set(LEVELS)
N_LEV = len(LEVELS)
_cnt = U.groupby(["parameter", "value"]).size()
N_REP = int(U["replicate"].max())
assert N_REP == 2 and (_cnt == N_REP).all() and len(_cnt) == N_LEV * N_P
N_RUNS2 = len(U)
N_SER = N_LEV * N_REP
N_SP2 = int((U["level"] == "set-point").sum())
for k in PK:
    _lv = U[U["parameter"] == k].groupby("level")["value"].first()
    assert (_lv["low"], _lv["high"], _lv["set-point"]) == (RNG[k][0], RNG[k][1], SP[k])
    assert np.isclose(_lv["low-mid"], (_lv["low"] + _lv["set-point"]) / 2)
    assert np.isclose(_lv["mid-high"], (_lv["set-point"] + _lv["high"]) / 2)
U["yield_pct"] = 100 * U["step_yield"]
_held = {c for c in UNIALL.columns[6:] if U[c].notna().all()}
assert _held == {"acidic_variants", "step_yield", "aggregate_out_pct", "residual_buffer_pct",
                 "ds_concentration_g_per_l"}
# the record holds no pH, conductivity series, load, permeate, duration or run-order result
assert not [c for c in U.columns if re.search(r"(^|_)ph($|_)", c) or "conduct" in c or "order" in c
            or "permeate" in c or "duration" in c or "pool_id" in c]
assert U[[c for c in U.columns if "load" in c]].isna().all().all()

RESP = ["aggregate_out_pct", "acidic_variants", "residual_buffer_pct", "yield_pct", "ds_concentration_g_per_l"]
RLAB = {"aggregate_out_pct": "Aggregates, HMW (%)", "acidic_variants": "Acidic variants (%)",
        "residual_buffer_pct": "Residual process buffer (%)", "yield_pct": "Step yield (%)",
        "ds_concentration_g_per_l": "Final concentration (g/L)"}
RDEC = {"aggregate_out_pct": 2, "acidic_variants": 1, "residual_buffer_pct": 4, "yield_pct": 1,
        "ds_concentration_g_per_l": 1}
ALPHA = float(THRESHOLDS["effect_alpha"])
AG, AC = "aggregate_out_pct", "acidic_variants"

def fit_line(k, r):
    g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    lr = sstat.linregress(g["value"], g[r])
    t = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, len(g) - 2)
    wd = RNG[k][1] - RNG[k][0]
    return dict(slope=lr.slope, ic=lr.intercept, se=lr.stderr, p=lr.pvalue,
                lo=lr.slope - t * lr.stderr, hi=lr.slope + t * lr.stderr, n=len(g), dfr=len(g) - 2,
                width=wd, ch=lr.slope * wd, ch_lo=(lr.slope - t * lr.stderr) * wd,
                ch_hi=(lr.slope + t * lr.stderr) * wd)

SL = {(k, r): fit_line(k, r) for k in PK for r in RESP}
SIG = {kr for kr, v in SL.items() if v["p"] < ALPHA}
assert SIG == {("diavolumes", "residual_buffer_pct"), ("tmp", AG), ("final_conc", AG),
               ("final_conc", "ds_concentration_g_per_l")}
N_SIG, N_SLOPES = len(SIG), len(SL)
SLDF = SL[("diavolumes", AG)]["dfr"]
sC, sT, sDV = SL[("final_conc", AG)], SL[("tmp", AG)], SL[("diavolumes", AG)]
assert sC["lo"] > 0 and sT["lo"] > 0 and sC["ch"] > sT["ch"]
CH_C_NOR = sC["slope"] * (NOR["final_conc"][1] - NOR["final_conc"][0])
CH_T_NOR = sT["slope"] * (NOR["tmp"][1] - NOR["tmp"][0])
# no slope of an attribute other than these two, and none of the step yield
assert not any((k, AC) in SIG for k in PK) and not any((k, "yield_pct") in SIG for k in PK)

def pooled_sd(r):
    grp = U.groupby(["parameter", "value"])[r]
    ss = float(((U[r] - grp.transform("mean")) ** 2).sum())
    dfp = len(U) - grp.ngroups
    return float(np.sqrt(ss / dfp)), int(dfp)

PE = {r: pooled_sd(r) for r in RESP}
PE_DF = PE[AG][1]
# PCP-010 §5.3: the rule for small changes and the slope test agree for aggregate, for every parameter
for k in PK:
    _s = SL[(k, AG)]
    assert (abs(_s["ch"]) > PE[AG][0]) == (_s["p"] < ALPHA)
MET = csv("dev_methods.csv").set_index("id")
ICIEF_LOQ = float(MET.loc["AMV-3013", "loq"])
A280_PREC = float(MET.loc["AMV-3019", "precision_pct"])
assert U[AC].min() > 10 * ICIEF_LOQ
AC_MEAN = float(U[AC].mean())

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ criteria and offsets
ACC_AG = D.effective_acceptance(UO, AG)
ACC_AC = D.effective_acceptance(UO, AC)
assert ACC_AG[2] == "upper" and ACC_AC[2] == "two_sided"
AG_HI = float(ACC_AG[1])
AC_LO, AC_HI = float(ACC_AC[0]), float(ACC_AC[1])
assert D.iac_table(UO).empty and D.rev1_criteria(UO).empty
assert D.acceptance_basis(UO, AG) == D.acceptance_basis(UO, AC) == "drug substance"
CRIT_AG = f"≤ {fg(AG_HI)} % HMW"
CRIT_AC = f"{fg(AC_LO)}–{fg(AC_HI)} %"
SDM_OUT = ["step_yield", AG, "ds_concentration_g_per_l", "flux_lmh"]
OFF = {r: D.sdm_offset(UO, r) for r in SDM_OUT}
assert all(o is not None and o["scale"] == "difference" for o in OFF.values())
assert all(o["lo"] < 0 < o["hi"] for o in OFF.values())              # every interval includes zero
assert OFF[AG]["offset"] > 0 and OFF["step_yield"]["offset"] < 0     # the direction the hold-up predicts
assert D.sdm_offset(UO, AC) is None and D.sdm_offset(UO, "residual_buffer_pct") is None
N_SD, N_M = OFF[AG]["n_sd"], OFF[AG]["n_m"]
assert all((o["n_sd"], o["n_m"]) == (N_SD, N_M) for o in OFF.values())
OFF_CI = int(round(100 * OFF[AG]["ci"]))
assert not T.sdm_offsets_data([UO])["judged"].any()

U["agg_mfg"] = D.to_mfg(UO, AG, U[AG].to_numpy(float))
with D.offset_at("lo"):
    AGG_AT_LO = np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, AG, U[AG].to_numpy(float)))
with D.offset_at("hi"):
    AGG_AT_HI = np.asarray(D.to_mfg(UO, AG, U[AG].to_numpy(float)))
U["in_nor"] = [(NOR[k][0] <= v) if ONE_SIDED[k] else (NOR[k][0] <= v <= NOR[k][1])
               for k, v in zip(U["parameter"], U["value"])]
_inn = U["in_nor"].to_numpy()
Q_AG = {"point": bool((U.loc[U["in_nor"], "agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all()),
        "lo": bool((AGG_AT_LO[_inn] <= AG_HI).all()), "hi": bool((AGG_AT_HI[_inn] <= AG_HI).all())}
QUAL_AG = len(set(Q_AG.values())) == 1
assert QUAL_AG and Q_AG["point"]
N_IN_NOR = int(_inn.sum())
AGG_NOR_WORST = float(max(AGG_AT_LO[_inn].max(), AGG_AT_HI[_inn].max(), U.loc[U["in_nor"], "agg_mfg"].max()))

SP2 = U[U["level"] == "set-point"]
AGG_SP2_MEAN = float(SP2[AG].mean())
AGG_SDM_MEAN, AGG_MFG_MEAN = OFF[AG]["mean_sd"], OFF[AG]["mean_m"]

AC_MET = bool(U[AC].between(AC_LO, AC_HI).all())
AG_MET = bool((U["agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all())
AG_MET_ENDS = bool((AGG_AT_LO <= AG_HI).all() and (AGG_AT_HI <= AG_HI).all())
assert AC_MET and AG_MET and AG_MET_ENDS
_i = U["agg_mfg"].idxmax()
AGG_MAX, AGG_MAX_K, AGG_MAX_V = float(U.loc[_i, "agg_mfg"]), U.loc[_i, "parameter"], float(U.loc[_i, "value"])
AGG_MARGIN = AG_HI - AGG_MAX
_i = U[AC].idxmin()
AC_MIN, AC_MIN_K, AC_MIN_V = float(U.loc[_i, AC]), U.loc[_i, "parameter"], float(U.loc[_i, "value"])
# runs that print as the lowest result at one decimal
AC_MIN_TIES = U[U[AC].round(1) == round(AC_MIN, 1)]
_i = U[AC].idxmax()
AC_MAX, AC_MAX_K, AC_MAX_V = float(U.loc[_i, AC]), U.loc[_i, "parameter"], float(U.loc[_i, "value"])
AC_MARGIN_LO, AC_MARGIN_HI = AC_MIN - AC_LO, AC_HI - AC_MAX
AC_CH_BOUND = max(max(abs(SL[(k, AC)]["ch_lo"]), abs(SL[(k, AC)]["ch_hi"])) for k in PK)
SHARE_C = 100 * sC["ch"] / AGG_MARGIN               # the larger aggregate change, against the margin
AC_CH_MAX_K = max(PK, key=lambda k: abs(SL[(k, AC)]["ch"]))
AC_CH_MAX = SL[(AC_CH_MAX_K, AC)]["ch"]
assert abs(AC_CH_MAX) > sC["ch"] and abs(AC_CH_MAX) < AC_MARGIN_LO
SHARE_C_CRIT = 100 * sC["ch"] / AG_HI

def where(k, v):
    if v == SP[k]:
        return f"at the set-point condition of the {nm[k]} series"
    return f"at {u_(k, v)} in the {nm[k]} series"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ PARs, edges, interaction bound
PARS = {}
for k in PK:
    g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    ok = {v: bool((h["agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all() and h[AC].between(AC_LO, AC_HI).all())
          for v, h in g.groupby("value")}
    vals = sorted(ok)
    i0 = vals.index(SP[k])
    assert ok[vals[i0]]
    a = i0
    while a > 0 and ok[vals[a - 1]]:
        a -= 1
    b = i0
    while b < len(vals) - 1 and ok[vals[b + 1]]:
        b += 1
    PARS[k] = (vals[a], vals[b])
assert all(PARS[k] == RNG[k] for k in PK)            # every PAR reaches both edges of the range studied
MARG = {k: (NOR[k][0] - PARS[k][0], None if ONE_SIDED[k] else PARS[k][1] - NOR[k][1]) for k in PK}
assert MARG["diavolumes"][0] == 0 and MARG["tmp"][0] == 0 and MARG["final_conc"][0] == MARG["final_conc"][1]

def marg_s(k, i):
    return "n.a." if MARG[k][i] is None else u_(k, MARG[k][i])
EDGE = U[U["level"].isin(["low", "high"])]
EDGE_AG_MARGIN = float(AG_HI - EDGE["agg_mfg"].max())
EDGE_AC_MARGIN = float(min(EDGE[AC].min() - AC_LO, AC_HI - EDGE[AC].max()))
# the corner argument is made per run: the highest set-point run at manufacturing scale plus the two slopes
SP_AGG_MFG_MAX = float(U.loc[U["level"] == "set-point", "agg_mfg"].max())
ADD_NOR = sC["slope"] * (NOR["final_conc"][1] - SP["final_conc"]) + sT["slope"] * (NOR["tmp"][1] - SP["tmp"])
ADD_RNG = sC["slope"] * (RNG["final_conc"][1] - SP["final_conc"]) + sT["slope"] * (RNG["tmp"][1] - SP["tmp"])
PRED_RNG = SP_AGG_MFG_MAX + ADD_RNG
GAP_RNG = AG_HI - PRED_RNG
RATIO_RNG = GAP_RNG / ADD_RNG
assert ADD_NOR > 0 and GAP_RNG > 0 and RATIO_RNG > 10

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the allowance at cation exchange
# PCMP-001 assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate. The verification at manufacturing
# scale (amab_process/iac.py, owner 2026-10-11) fits aggregate of S-UFDF-UNI2, offset applied, on the
# three parameters with all runs pooled and no interaction, and takes the one-sided 95 % prediction bound
# of a single run at the least favourable NOR combination, minus the fitted set-point mean.
VER = D.iac_verification(UO)
assert len(VER) == 1
VER = VER.iloc[0]
assert VER["cqa"] == "aggregates_hmw" and VER["assumption"] == "add_max" and float(VER["assumed"]) == 0.0
assert not bool(VER["met"]) and VER["offset_scale"] == "difference"
assert np.isclose(float(VER["offset"]), OFF[AG]["offset"], atol=1e-3)
UF_ALLOW = float(VER["predicted_nor_bound95"])
UF_WORST_MEAN = float(VER["predicted_nor"])
_ir = csv("iac.csv")
_ir = _ir[(_ir["step_key"] == "cex") & (_ir["response"] == AG)].iloc[0]
assert bool(_ir["tightened"]) and not bool(_ir["widened"])
assert float(_ir["iac_high_apriori"]) == AG_HI and np.isclose(float(_ir["iac_high"]), CEX_AG)
assert np.isclose(float(_ir["downstream_added"]), UF_ALLOW, atol=1e-3)
assert np.isclose(AG_HI - UF_ALLOW, CEX_AG, atol=1e-3) and CEX_AG < AG_HI
assert 0 < UF_WORST_MEAN < UF_ALLOW
UF_GAP, UF_PLOF = float(VER["r2_minus_pred_r2"]), float(VER["p_lack_of_fit"])
assert bool(VER["model_adequate"]) and UF_GAP <= float(THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"])
assert UF_PLOF > float(THRESHOLDS["lof_alpha"])
# the F-test of the same main-effects fit (criterion 1 of PCMP-001 §7.2), which iac_verification.csv does not carry
from amab_process import adequacy as ADQ
_vd = U[["parameter", "value", "agg_mfg"]].copy()
for k in PK:
    _nat = np.where(_vd["parameter"] == k, _vd["value"].astype(float), SP[k])
    _vd["coded_" + k] = (_nat - (RNG[k][0] + RNG[k][1]) / 2) / ((RNG[k][1] - RNG[k][0]) / 2)
_va = ADQ.adequacy(_vd.reset_index(drop=True), "agg_mfg", PK, PK,
                   {k_: float(v_) for k_, v_ in THRESHOLDS.items()}, block=False)
assert np.isclose(_va["gap"], UF_GAP, atol=1e-3) and np.isclose(_va["p_lof"], UF_PLOF, atol=1e-3)
assert _va["f_ok"] and _va["adequate"]
UF_PF = float(_va["p"])
# the one-sided NOR of the diavolumes: the simulation and the combinations use NOR high (amab_process.studies
# _sample_overrides, amab_process.iac _univariate_increase)
DV_SIM_SD = (NOR["diavolumes"][1] - NOR["diavolumes"][0]) / 6
DV_COMBO_HI = NOR["diavolumes"][1]
assert NOR["diavolumes"][0] < SP["diavolumes"] < DV_COMBO_HI < RNG["diavolumes"][1]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ buffer exchange
G = U[U["parameter"] == "diavolumes"]
_lrb = sstat.linregress(G["value"], np.log(G["residual_buffer_pct"]))
_tb = sstat.t.ppf(0.975, len(G) - 2)
RB_B, RB_IC = _lrb.slope, _lrb.intercept
RB_LO, RB_HI = RB_B - _tb * _lrb.stderr, RB_B + _tb * _lrb.stderr
RB_R2 = _lrb.rvalue ** 2
assert RB_LO < -1 < RB_HI                            # consistent with exp(-DV)
RB_FOLD = float(np.exp(-RB_B))
RB_REMOVED = 100 * (1 - np.exp(RB_B))
RB = G.groupby("value")["residual_buffer_pct"].agg(["min", "max", "mean"])
_dvs = list(RB.index)
assert all(RB.loc[a_, "min"] > RB.loc[b_, "max"] for a_, b_ in zip(_dvs[:-1], _dvs[1:]))   # no plateau
RB_NORLO, RB_SP, RB_TOP = RB.loc[NOR["diavolumes"][0]], RB.loc[SP["diavolumes"]], RB.loc[RNG["diavolumes"][1]]

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ step yield and final concentration
Y_MEAN, Y_MIN, Y_MAX = U["yield_pct"].mean(), U["yield_pct"].min(), U["yield_pct"].max()
FC = U[U["parameter"] == "final_conc"]
FC_DIFF_MAX = float((FC["ds_concentration_g_per_l"] - FC["value"]).abs().max())
FC_OTH = U.loc[U["parameter"] != "final_conc", "ds_concentration_g_per_l"]
assert FC_OTH.between(*NOR["final_conc"]).all()
sFC = SL[("final_conc", "ds_concentration_g_per_l")]
A280_SD_AT_TARGET = A280_PREC / 100 * DS_TARGET

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ study events
DEV1_EFFECT_HI = sT["hi"] * (dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi - SP["tmp"])     # upper end of the two-sided 95 % CI
DEV1_SHIFT = DEV1_EFFECT_HI / N_SD
assert AGG_NOR_WORST + DEV1_SHIFT <= AG_HI
# DEV-010-02: the further concentration may have raised the aggregate of its run. If that run was a
# scale-down run of S-UFDF-SDM it entered the aggregate offset: the offset with any one run left out.
_sdq = csv("sdm_qualification.csv")
_sdq = _sdq[(_sdq["step"] == UO) & (_sdq["study"] == SDM_ID)]
_sdv = _sdq.loc[_sdq["scale"] == "scale-down", AG].to_numpy(float)
_mv = float(_sdq.loc[_sdq["scale"] == "manufacturing", AG].mean())
assert len(_sdv) == N_SD and np.isclose(_sdv.mean() - _mv, OFF[AG]["offset"])
OFF_DROP = [float(np.delete(_sdv, _j).mean() - _mv) for _j in range(len(_sdv))]
OFF_DROP_LO, OFF_DROP_HI = min(OFF_DROP), max(OFF_DROP)
AGG_MAX_DROP = float(U[AG].max() - OFF_DROP_LO)
AGG_MARGIN_DROP = AG_HI - AGG_MAX_DROP
assert OFF_DROP_LO < OFF[AG]["offset"] < OFF_DROP_HI and AGG_MAX_DROP < AG_HI

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ capability (integrated model)
CAPT = cap.set_index("key")
POOS = D.p_oos().set_index("key")
MC = csv("monte_carlo.csv")
N_MC = int(V["n_monte_carlo"])
assert len(MC) == N_MC and (CAPT.loc[["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"], "n"] == N_MC).all()
CPK_AG = float(CAPT.loc["aggregates_hmw", "Cpk"])
CPK_AC = float(CAPT.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpk"])
CPK_DNA = float(CAPT.loc["residual_dna", "Cpk"])
assert CPK_AG >= CPK_TARGET and CPK_DNA >= CPK_TARGET and CPK_MIN <= CPK_AC < CPK_TARGET
assert CAPT.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpl"] < CAPT.loc["acidic_variants", "Cpu"]    # the lower end limits it
assert CPK_AC < min(CPK_AG, CPK_DNA)
assert CAPT.loc["residual_dna", "unit"] == "ng/dose"
NOOS = {k: int(POOS.loc[k, "n_oos"]) for k in ["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"]}
assert NOOS["aggregates_hmw"] == 0 and NOOS["residual_dna"] == 0 and NOOS["acidic_variants"] >= 1
PPM = {k: float(POOS.loc[k, "ppm_normal"]) for k in NOOS}
MCS = {k: (float(MC[k].mean()), float(MC[k].std(ddof=1))) for k in NOOS}
for k in NOOS:
    assert abs(MCS[k][0] - float(CAPT.loc[k, "mean"])) < 1e-3
DNA_CRIT = float(CAPT.loc["residual_dna", "acc_high"])
DNA_MEAN = MCS["residual_dna"][0]
DNA_PG = DNA_MEAN * 1000.0 / DOSE_MG
assert np.isclose(dna_ng_per_dose(DNA_PG), DNA_MEAN)
assert MET.loc["AMV-3014", "loq_unit"] == "pg/mg"
DNA_LOQ = float(MET.loc["AMV-3014", "loq"])
DNA_LOQ_RATIO = DNA_LOQ / DNA_PG
assert DNA_LOQ_RATIO > 1000
DNA_LOQ_RATIO_S = f"{float(f'{DNA_LOQ_RATIO:.2g}'):,.0f}"      # two significant figures
N_MC_S = f"{N_MC:,}"
P_UB_PCT = 100 * (1 - 0.05 ** (1 / N_MC))     # one-sided 95 % bound, no batch outside in N_MC

# the measured acidic variants of S-UFDF-UNI2 against the simulated drug substance (content review Q5.2)
AC_SIM_MEAN, AC_SIM_SD = MCS["acidic_variants"]
assert U[AC].max() < AC_SIM_MEAN                      # every measured result lies below the simulated mean
CPK_AC_MEAS = (AC_MEAN - AC_LO) / (3 * AC_SIM_SD)     # at the mean of the study, with the simulated spread
assert CPK_AC_MEAS < CPK_MIN

def span(lo, hi, d):
    """A range of two results, or one value when both print the same."""
    a_, b_ = fx(lo, d), fx(hi, d)
    return a_ if a_ == b_ else f"{a_}–{b_}"

def verdict(c):
    if c >= CPK_TARGET:
        return "At or above the target"
    return "Between the minimum and the target" if c >= CPK_MIN else "Below the minimum"
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

Ultrafiltration and diafiltration (UF/DF) is Step `{python} STEP_N`, the last step of the A-Mab drug substance process. It concentrates the antibody, exchanges the process buffer for the formulation buffer and delivers the drug substance at its target concentration of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")`. This report gives the results of the characterization of the step under the plan PCP-010 and the master plan PCMP-001. It is part of the Stage 1 record that supports the transfer of the process from the development site in `{python} SENDING_LOCATION` to the commercial drug substance site in `{python} RECEIVING_LOCATION`.

The step has no designed experiment. The risk assessment RA-001 assigned its `{python} w(N_P)` parameters, the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, the `{python} nm["tmp"]` (TMP) and the `{python} nm["final_conc"]`, to univariate study. Version 1.0 of this report described the planned univariate study `{python} UNI_ID` without a result for any parameter effect. The results reported here come from a further univariate study, `{python} UNI2_ID`, made from `{python} UNI2_START` to `{python} UNI2_END`, after the QA investigation INV-001 had closed. Each parameter was run at `{python} w(N_LEV)` levels across its range studied, in duplicate, with the other parameters at their set-points. The study ran on a second tangential flow filtration (TFF) skid, `{python} UNI2_EQ`. The offsets of the scale-down model from manufacturing scale were measured on the first skid, `{python} SDM_EQ`, and no run compared the two skids. The offsets are applied to the results of the second skid, because the two skids share their design and their membrane and the offsets are small against the criteria (`{python} PD1`).

Every result met the drug substance criteria for aggregate (`{python} CRIT_AG`) and for the acidic charge variants (`{python} CRIT_AC`), at every level of every parameter. The proven acceptable range (PAR) of each parameter is therefore its range studied, `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")`, `{python} rng_s("tmp")` and `{python} rng_s("final_conc")`. Aggregate in the final retentate rose with the final DS concentration (`{python} pe(sC["p"])`) and with TMP (`{python} pe(sT["p"])`). Across the ranges studied the two effects amount to `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` and `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points, and the highest result lay `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion. The A-Mab case study leaves UF/DF out, so no published source gave the size of this effect in advance. No effect of the number of diavolumes on aggregate was detected, and no slope of the acidic charge variants was significant.

PCMP-001 assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate. A check of that assumption on `{python} UNI2_ID` found a rise of aggregate across the NORs of UF/DF of up to `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points, at the one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single run (`{python} PD[8]`). This prediction bound of the aggregate rise across the step tightens the aggregate criterion of the cation exchange pool from `{python} fx(AG_HI)` to `{python} fx(CEX_AG)` % HMW.

The residual process buffer fell by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume, the fall expected when the buffer species pass the membrane freely. At the minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])` it was at most `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` % of the process buffer. The buffer-exchange criterion of PCP-010 rests on conductivity readings that are not in the study record, so it could not be judged as planned. The buffer exchange is controlled instead by its minimum number of diavolumes, and the formulation buffer of the drug substance is confirmed against its release limits (`{python} PD[7]`).

All `{python} w(N_P)` parameters were classified as key process parameters (KPPs), and the step has no critical process parameter. In the integrated process model of `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches the drug substance has a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)` for aggregate, `{python} fx(CPK_AC)` for the acidic charge variants and `{python} fx(CPK_DNA, 1)` for residual DNA, which is judged in ng per dose. The Cpk of the acidic charge variants lies between the minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)` and the target of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` set by PCMP-001. It is set by the distance from the simulated mean to the lower limit of `{python} fg(AC_LO)` %. This step can only raise the acidic charge variants, by deamidation, so it moves them away from that limit. Every result of this study lies below the simulated mean. At the mean of the study, with the simulated standard deviation, the Cpk would be `{python} fx(CPK_AC_MEAS)`, below the minimum, so this report cannot confirm the simulated capability from its own results (@sec-capability). Version 1.0 recorded two study events, a TMP excursion to `{python} u_("tmp", dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi)` (DEV-010-01) and a final concentration of `{python} u_("final_conc", dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l)` before a further concentration (DEV-010-02). Neither changes a conclusion. The ranges and classes of this report roll up into the master report PCMR-001.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Product and unit operation {#sec-product}

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody [@amab2009]. Its drug substance is purified by the platform train of Protein A capture, low-pH viral inactivation, cation exchange, anion exchange, small virus retentive filtration and UF/DF. UF/DF is the last step of the train, and its product is the drug substance. The commercial process runs at a production bioreactor working volume of `{python} SCALE_L` L.

The step works across a tangential flow membrane whose pores pass buffer salts and retain the antibody. Ultrafiltration removes permeate and raises the antibody concentration in the retentate. Diafiltration then adds formulation buffer at the rate at which permeate leaves, so that the retentate volume stays constant while the permeable species are washed out. A second concentration brings the retentate to the drug substance target, and a buffer flush recovers it. The step is operated under SOP-2013.

The step is not expected to change the glycan variants of A-Mab, and it is credited with no clearance of host cell protein, DNA or leached Protein A. No viral clearance is claimed for it. It can add to aggregate, which can form at the membrane wall and in the recirculation pump. It can also add to the acidic charge variants, because deamidation continues while the antibody is in solution on the skid (@sec-prior). Aggregate and the acidic charge variants are therefore the attributes measured across the step. The residual process buffer, the step yield and the final concentration are measures of process performance.

@tbl-related lists the documents to which this report is related. The paired plan is PCP-010, and the parameters were assigned to their studies by the risk assessment RA-001.

## Objectives {#sec-objectives}

PCP-010 set the studies the following objectives.

(i) To estimate the offsets of a bench-scale TFF model of the commercial skid from manufacturing scale, as the basis of its qualification (PCMP-001 §7.1).
(ii) To determine the effect of the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, the TMP and the `{python} nm["final_conc"]` on aggregate and on the acidic charge variants of the drug substance, over the ranges studied.
(iii) To establish the number of diavolumes at which the retentate reaches the formulation buffer, so that the lower edge of the operating range rests on data for A-Mab and not on platform practice alone.
(iv) To establish a PAR for each parameter against the drug substance criteria for aggregate and the acidic charge variants.
(v) To provide the evidence on which the parameters are classified under SOP-4001, and to carry that classification into the control strategy through this report and the master report PCMR-001.

@sec-conclusions states the outcome of each objective.

## Regulatory and scientific basis {#sec-basis}

The study follows the lifecycle approach to process validation, and this report is part of the record of Stage 1, process design [@fda2011]. Development follows the enhanced approach of ICH Q8(R2) and ICH Q11, with criticality treated as a continuum and risk managed under ICH Q9 [@ichq8; @ichq11; @ichq9]. The criticality of the attributes and the logic of parameter classification come from the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. The case study leaves UF/DF out of its characterization [@amab2009, p. 114], so it gives no expectation and no result for this step. Viral safety rests on the modular and orthogonal clearance of low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration [@ichq5a]. This step contributes no log reduction to it, and the cumulative claim is consolidated in PCMR-001.

## Changes in this revision {#sec-changes}

Version 1.0 of this report was approved on `{python} rev1_date(DOC)`. Version 2.0 is issued under the QA investigation INV-001. QA opened it on `{python} INV["opened"]`, after its review of the master report PCMR-001 Version 1.0 for BLA readiness, and closed it on `{python} INV["closed"]`. INV-001 found that the criteria used to judge each step in the PAR analysis had been set after the data were seen and appeared in no approved plan (INV-001 finding 1). The master plan PCMP-001 was reissued as Version 2.0 with criteria derived a priori, and PCP-010 was amended to apply it. This report states its results against the amended plan. The changes are the following.

1. Version 1.0 described the planned univariate study `{python} UNI_ID` and its outcome, but gave no result for any parameter effect. This version reports `{python} UNI2_ID`, a further univariate study made during the re-analysis, and every effect, PAR and class in it rests on that study (@sec-univariate). The plan did not foresee the study, and @sec-discrepancies records it as `{python} PD1`.
2. The acidic charge variants are judged against both ends of their criterion of `{python} CRIT_AC`. Version 1.0 read them against the upper limit of `{python} fg(AC_HI)` % alone (INV-001 finding 4), although Version 1.0 of the plan stated the two-sided criterion. The capability of the drug substance is now also assessed against both ends (@sec-capability).
3. The criteria at this step are the drug substance criteria, which Version 1.0 of the plan also stated. No step follows UF/DF, so PCMP-001 defines no intermediate acceptance criterion (IAC) for it (@sec-basis-par).
4. The scale-down model is judged by its offsets from manufacturing scale (PCMP-001 §7.1), in place of the tests for a significant difference of Version 1.0. @sec-sdm states the approach this report takes to the qualification decision at a step without a response-surface model.
5. The execution window of each study and the calibration status of the skid it used are given (@sec-sdm, @sec-univariate). This answers INV-001 finding 5, that the Version 1.0 records gave no execution dates.
6. The events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded as deviations are called study events, because a process characterization study is not GMP manufacture. They keep their numbers DEV-010-01 and DEV-010-02 (@sec-events).
7. The parameters are classified under the rules of PCMP-001 Version 2.0. An attribute is affected by a parameter when its slope is significant (PCMP-001 §6.2), and a significant effect too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make the parameter critical (PCMP-001 §7.7). @sec-classification applies both rules.
8. The capability section gives the probability that the drug substance is out of specification, and it judges residual DNA in ng per dose (@sec-capability).
9. The NOR of the number of diavolumes is a minimum, at least `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. The step counts diavolumes to its set-point and is not run below the minimum (@sec-factors).
10. The buffer exchange is judged on the minimum number of diavolumes and on the release of the drug substance against the limits of its formulation buffer, because the conductivity readings on which PCP-010 judges it are not in the study record (@sec-buffer).
11. The rise of aggregate across the NORs of this step is carried into the criterion of the cation exchange pool, which is tightened from `{python} fx(AG_HI)` to `{python} fx(CEX_AG)` % HMW (@sec-basis-par).

Two statements of Version 1.0 are reversed. Version 1.0 stated that no effect of any parameter on product quality was detected over the ranges assessed. Aggregate rises with the final DS concentration and with TMP (@sec-aggregate). Version 1.0 also stated that both edges of the diavolume range leave the residual process buffer "far below what the formulation tolerates". The study record holds no limit for what the formulation tolerates, and this version makes no such claim (@sec-buffer).

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior-basis}

## Platform and prior-product knowledge {#sec-prior}

The step belongs to the platform train that was used for X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab (PCMP-001 §2). The places where aggregate can form in the step are the same for every antibody, so that experience applies to the qualitative behaviour of the step. How readily an antibody aggregates depends on its colloidal stability and its self-association, which differ between antibodies. The viscosity of the retentate rises with concentration and differs between antibodies too. For this reason the final DS concentration was studied for A-Mab and was not carried over from the platform. The A-Mab case study leaves the step out [@amab2009, p. 114]. The expectations below therefore come from general knowledge of the tangential flow filtration of antibodies, as PCP-010 §4.1 records them.

Each diavolume removes a fixed fraction of the permeable species that remain in the retentate. PCP-010 §4.1 expects the residual process buffer components to fall "roughly exponentially" with the number of diavolumes. At high antibody concentration two effects can hold the retentate off the composition of the buffer. The antibody carries a net charge, so buffer ions of the opposite charge are enriched in the retentate and ions of the same charge are depleted (the Donnan effect). The antibody also occupies part of the retentate volume, which lowers the concentration of each excipient in the retentate as a whole (volume exclusion). Both effects can move the pH and the excipient levels of the retentate away from the values of the buffer.

The membrane retains the antibody, so the antibody accumulates at the membrane wall in a polarization layer, where its concentration is higher than in the bulk retentate. The retentate also passes many times through the recirculation pump. Aggregate can form at the wall, where the antibody is most concentrated, and in the pump, where cavitation, air-liquid interfaces and particles shed by the pump can start it. Shear alone causes little aggregation of an antibody. Aggregate was therefore expected to rise with the final DS concentration, which raises the concentration in the bulk retentate and, below the limiting flux, at the wall. The limiting flux is the flux beyond which a higher pressure no longer raises the permeate rate. Below it, a higher TMP drives more permeate through the membrane and raises the antibody concentration at the wall. Above it, the concentration at the wall stays at its limiting value. A higher TMP then compacts and thickens the polarization layer, with no gain in flux, so more antibody is held at that concentration. Aggregate was therefore expected to rise with TMP below the limiting flux, and it may still rise above it. It was also expected to rise with the number of passes through the pump, which more diavolumes increase. Within the normal operating ranges (NORs) the exposure is short, and the effects were expected to be small. No source gave their size for A-Mab, so this study measures it (@sec-aggregate). The effect of a high final DS concentration and a high TMP on aggregate is this campaign's own addition to the integrated process model (@sec-stats).

Deamidation of asparagine residues continues while the antibody is in solution. It converts a neutral residue into a charged one, so it can only raise the acidic charge variants. The increase grows with the time in solution, at a rate that rises with pH and temperature. The operation lasts longer with more diavolumes, with a higher final concentration, which lowers the flux, and with a lower TMP below the limiting flux. The acidic charge variants were therefore expected to rise, if at all, with the number of diavolumes and the final DS concentration, and to fall with TMP.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

@tbl-cqas lists the attributes in scope at this step, with their drug substance criteria and the criticality assigned with Tool #1 of the A-Mab case study, the product of impact and uncertainty [@amab2009]. The studies measured aggregate and the acidic charge variants in the final retentate. Both arrive with the load, and both are formed first in the production bioreactor. Deamidation continues wherever the antibody is held in solution, aggregate also forms at the low-pH elution and hold, and the cation exchange step reduces aggregate (PCMP-001 §5 and Table 7.1). Residual DNA is in scope as an attribute of the drug substance that this step delivers. It is not measured across the step and has no intermediate criterion, so it is judged on the drug substance in the integrated process model (PCMP-001 §7.3, @sec-capability).

```{python}
#| output: asis
_cq = cqas_by_keys(["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"]).reset_index(drop=True)
_cq["Tool #1"] = _cq["Tool #1"].astype(int).astype(str)
_cq["At this step"] = ["Measured in the final retentate by SEC",
                       "Measured in the final retentate by icIEF",
                       "Not measured. Judged on the drug substance in the integrated process model"]
_cq = _cq.rename(columns={"Acceptance": "Drug substance\ncriterion"})
T.frame(_cq, "Quality attributes in scope at the step, with their drug substance criteria and criticality.",
        "tbl-cqas", align=["P{3.3cm}", "P{2.1cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "c", "c", "P{4.4cm}"],
        notes=[("", "H, high criticality. VL, very low criticality. Tool #1, the impact of the attribute on "
                    "safety and efficacy multiplied by the uncertainty of that impact (A-Mab attribute "
```

The other attributes of the drug substance register are not measured across the step. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose are formed in the production bioreactor. The membrane retains the antibody whatever its glycoform, so the step is not expected to change their distribution, and they were not measured. Host cell protein and leached Protein A are cleared by the chromatography steps before this one, and PCMP-001 Table 7.1 credits UF/DF with no clearance of either. Fragments form by proteolytic clipping of the antibody in culture and during the harvest hold, and slowly by hydrolysis of the hinge region in solution. Version 1.0 left fragments out of the studies of this step, and PCP-010 keeps that scope. PCMP-001 Table 7.1 assumes that this step does not change fragments, and the drug substance is tested for fragments at release. Viral clearance is credited to low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration and is not measured here.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection {#sec-risk}

RA-001 ranked every process parameter of the drug substance process for its potential impact on the CQAs and on process performance, and for its potential to interact with other parameters [@ichq9]. Parameters ranked high, or with a likely interaction, were assigned to multivariate study. Parameters ranked lower, whose range could be supported one factor at a time, were assigned to univariate study (PCMP-001 §4). All `{python} w(N_P)` parameters of UF/DF were assigned to univariate study, and no designed experiment was planned for the step.

A higher TMP and a higher final DS concentration both raise the antibody concentration in the polarization layer at the membrane wall, or compact that layer once the flux has reached its limit. A higher final DS concentration raises the viscosity and the bulk concentration of the retentate, and both lower the limiting flux. The flux then reaches its limit at a lower TMP, and above that TMP a higher pressure compacts the layer. The rise of aggregate with TMP may therefore be larger at a high final DS concentration than at a low one. A study that varies one factor at a time cannot resolve such an interaction. It bounds the effect of each parameter at the edge of its range studied, with the others at their set-points (@sec-pars). PCP-010 §4.3 keeps the rule of Version 1.0 that runs with two parameters at their range edges together are made where a measured attribute approaches its criterion at an edge. Such runs are made before a range is claimed, and they are agreed with Statistics and QA before they are executed.

# Materials and methods {#sec-mm}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

The bench-scale model holds the crossflow and the membrane loading at their commercial values, both scaled by membrane area (PCMP-001 §5). The membrane chemistry, the nominal molecular weight cut-off and the feed channel geometry are those of the commercial skid. The TMP, the number of diavolumes and the final concentration do not depend on scale and were set at the values under study. One quantity cannot be matched, the share of the batch held up in the system. With the crossflow and the membrane loading matched per unit area, the antibody passes through the pump as often at bench scale as at commercial scale. The bench skid, however, holds a larger share of its batch in its recirculation loop and has a larger ratio of surface to volume. More antibody is therefore lost to hold-up, and more of it meets surfaces and air-liquid interfaces per gram processed. A slightly lower step yield and slightly more aggregate were expected at bench scale.

The qualification study `{python} SDM_ID` ran from `{python} SDM_START` to `{python} SDM_END` on the skid `{python} SDM_EQ`, under SOP-1001. It compared `{python} w(N_SD)` runs of the model at the set-point condition with `{python} w(N_M)` batches at manufacturing scale. The outputs compared were the step yield, the aggregate content of the final retentate, the final concentration achieved and the permeate flux at the set-point TMP of `{python} sp_s("tmp")`. @tbl-sdm-runs gives the individual runs. The scale-down runs were complete on `{python} SDM_END`, before the first characterization run of the step on `{python} UNI_START`, as PCMP-001 §7.1 requires. The qualification record numbers the manufacturing-scale batches without naming them, and it gives no date for the calculation of the offsets. PCP-010 §5.1 asks this report to give both, and @sec-discrepancies records the gap as `{python} PD[5]`.

Under PCMP-001 §7.1 the offset of an output is the mean of the scale-down runs at set-point minus the mean of the manufacturing-scale batches, with its two-sided `{python} OFF_CI` % confidence interval. @tbl-sdm-offsets gives the four offsets. The bench skid gave a mean aggregate `{python} fx(OFF[AG]["offset"])` percentage points higher and a mean step yield `{python} fx(-100 * OFF["step_yield"]["offset"], 1)` percentage points lower than manufacturing scale. Both differences are in the direction that the larger hold-up predicts. Each interval includes zero, and so do the intervals of the final concentration and the permeate flux. Each interval rests on `{python} w(N_SD)` runs against `{python} w(N_M)` batches and is wide, so this report uses the ends of the interval and not its inclusion of zero.

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sdm_offsets([UO]).show()
```

Of the four outputs only aggregate carries a criterion at this step. The offsets of the step yield, the final concentration and the permeate flux are recorded, and no conclusion depends on them (PCMP-001 §7.1). The qualification compared the aggregate content of the final retentate and not the change in aggregate across the step that PCP-010 Table 5.1 names, because no load was sampled (@sec-sampling, `{python} PD[5]`). The aggregate offset is therefore subtracted directly from each aggregate result of the final retentate. Every comparison of aggregate with its criterion in this report is stated at manufacturing scale.

Under PCMP-001 §7.1 the decision whether a model is qualified for an output is made on the response-surface model of the step. This step has none. @tbl-sdm-offsets marks that decision as not applicable, and PCP-010 §7.1 leaves the decision to this report (`{python} PD[6]`). This report keeps the logic of PCMP-001 §7.1, that a model is qualified for an output when the conclusion over the NOR is the same with the offset at its estimate and at either end of its interval. Without a model, the conclusion over the NOR is whether every individual aggregate result at a level inside the NOR meets the criterion at manufacturing scale. All `{python} N_IN_NOR` aggregate results inside the NOR met the criterion in all three cases, so the model is qualified for aggregate under this approach. The highest of them was `{python} fx(AGG_NOR_WORST)` % HMW, with the offset at the end of its interval that is least favourable to the criterion.

The univariate study `{python} UNI2_ID` ran on the second skid `{python} UNI2_EQ`. The qualification measured the offsets on `{python} SDM_EQ` only, and no run compared the two skids. The offsets of `{python} SDM_EQ` are applied to the results of `{python} UNI2_EQ` (`{python} PD1`). This is accepted on two grounds. The two skids share their design and their membrane, so the hold-up and the surface that the antibody meets per gram, which cause the offsets, are expected to be alike. The offsets are also small against the criteria. The aggregate offset is `{python} fx(OFF[AG]["offset"])` percentage points, and the highest aggregate result of `{python} UNI2_ID` lies `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below its criterion (@sec-criteria). As measured, the `{python} w(N_SP2)` set-point runs of `{python} UNI2_ID` gave a mean aggregate of `{python} fx(AGG_SP2_MEAN)` %, against `{python} fx(AGG_SDM_MEAN)` % for the scale-down runs of `{python} SDM_ID` and `{python} fx(AGG_MFG_MEAN)` % for the manufacturing-scale batches.

The acidic charge variants and the residual process buffer were not compared at both scales. Their offsets are unknown, not zero, and both are judged as measured (PCMP-001 §7.1). For the acidic charge variants this rests on the kinetics of deamidation, which depend on the pH and the temperature of the solution and on the time spent in it, and not on the scale of the skid. At the same TMP and crossflow the flux is the same at both scales, so a run of the model lasts as long as the commercial step at the same settings (PCP-010 §5.1). For the buffer exchange it rests on the passage of the buffer species through the membrane. That passage is a property of the membrane and of the species, so the fraction removed in each diavolume does not depend on scale.

## Operation {#sec-operation}

The step receives the filtrate pool of the small virus retentive filtration step. Under SOP-2013 the pool is concentrated by ultrafiltration, diafiltered at constant volume against formulation buffer for the number of diavolumes of the run, concentrated a second time to the final target and recovered with a buffer flush. At the set-point condition the step runs `{python} sp_s("diavolumes")` at a TMP of `{python} sp_s("tmp")` to a final concentration of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")`. The composition of the formulation buffer is fixed by the drug product program and was a constant of the studies. Under PCP-010 §5.2 every run is loaded from a single pool of the virus filtration step, so that the variability of the load does not confound the comparison between levels. Section 12 of the plan gives a bridging rule if one pool is not sufficient. The study record of `{python} UNI2_ID` does not identify the load pool of its runs, so it cannot show that one pool served the whole study (`{python} PD[4]`).

## Analytical methods {#sec-methods}

The procedures and validated methods are listed in @tbl-sops. Aggregate is measured by size exclusion chromatography (SEC) under AMV-3011 and reported as the percentage of high molecular weight species (HMW). The acidic charge variants are measured by imaged capillary isoelectric focusing (icIEF) under AMV-3013 and reported as the percentage of acidic species. Protein concentration is measured by ultraviolet absorbance (A280) under AMV-3019, and the final concentration and the step yield rest on that measurement. PCP-010 follows the buffer exchange by the conductivity and the pH of the retentate, which are in-process readings of the skid instrumentation and not validated assays. The study record of `{python} UNI2_ID` gives one result of the buffer exchange per run, the residual process buffer. This is the part of the process buffer, the buffer in which the antibody enters the step, that is left in the final retentate, given as a percentage. The record names neither the buffer species measured nor the method, and it holds no conductivity or pH reading (`{python} PD[2]`).

```{python}
#| output: asis
T.sop_references(sops=UFDF_SOP_REFS, amvs=UFDF_AMV_REFS).show()
```

The studies of this step do not measure fragments, a scope that PCP-010 keeps from Version 1.0. The analytical method decision AMD-001 of `{python} AMD["date"]` set non-reduced CE-SDS (nrCE-SDS) as the method for fragments at every step, so it changes no result of this report. AMD-001 moved fragments away from SEC because host cell protein that elutes in the low molecular weight window of SEC is counted as fragment. No such interference applies to aggregate, and SEC remains its method (PCMP-001 §7.8). Aggregate was measured by SEC in the qualification study `{python} SDM_ID` and in the univariate study `{python} UNI2_ID` (PCP-010 §5.3).

The aggregate content of A-Mab drug substance is low, and a change across this step may be of the size of the repeatability of SEC. PCP-010 §5.3 keeps the rules of Version 1.0 for such small changes. A measured change is judged against the pure error of the study and not against the nominal precision of the method. Noise near the low end of the method range is attributed to the assay unless the change measured across the range is larger than the pure error. @sec-stats states how this rule and the slope test were applied together. PCP-010 §5.3 also asks for the variability of each method over the range of the samples. The study record reports none, so the pure error of the duplicate runs is the only measure of variability used here (`{python} PD[4]`).

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

@tbl-sampling compares the samples that PCP-010 Table 5.2 planned with the results that the record of `{python} UNI2_ID` holds. The criteria for aggregate and the acidic charge variants apply to the final retentate, and the record holds both results for every run, together with the final concentration and the step yield. It holds one result of the residual process buffer per run and no conductivity or pH reading (`{python} PD[2]`). The load pool, the pre-diafiltration retentate and the permeate were not sampled (`{python} PD[3]`). Without a load result the change in aggregate and in the acidic charge variants across the step cannot be calculated. The study therefore measures how the parameters change the final retentate, and not what the step adds to its load. Without a permeate result the retention of the antibody by the membrane is not confirmed either.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_smp = pd.DataFrame([
    ["Load pool", "Virus filtration filtrate, before ultrafiltration", "A280, SEC, icIEF", "None"],
    ["Pre-diafiltration retentate", "End of the first concentration", "A280", "None"],
    ["Diafiltration series", "After each diavolume, in the runs of the diavolume series", "Conductivity, pH",
     "One residual process buffer result per run. No conductivity or pH reading"],
    ["Final retentate", "After the final concentration and the recovery flush", "A280, SEC, icIEF",
     "Final concentration, aggregate and acidic charge variants in every run, with the step yield "
     "from the mass balance"],
    ["Permeate", "Composite over the run", "A280", "None"]],
    columns=["Sample", "Point in the step", "Tests planned\nin PCP-010", f"Results in the record\nof {UNI2_ID}"])
T.frame(_smp, f"Samples planned in PCP-010 and results held in the record of {UNI2_ID}.", "tbl-sampling",
        align=["P{2.7cm}", "P{3.8cm}", "P{2.4cm}", "P{5.6cm}"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Conductivity and pH are in-process readings of the skid instrumentation, not validated "
                    "assays (PCP-010 §5.3).")]).show()
```

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

For each parameter and each output, the individual results were regressed on the setting of the parameter over the range studied, and the slope was tested against zero at α = `{python} fg(ALPHA)` (PCP-010 §5.5, PCMP-001 §6.2). Each series has `{python} N_SER` runs, so each slope has `{python} SLDF` degrees of freedom. An attribute is called affected by a parameter when its slope is significant at that level. The change across the range studied is the slope times the width of the range. It is reported with its 95 % confidence interval beside the p-value, so that statistical and practical significance are read apart. The criterion, and not the p-value, decides whether a range is acceptable. No response-surface model was fitted, because the study has no factorial structure and no interaction can be estimated from it. The model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2 apply to response-surface models and not to these slopes. The one fit of several parameters in this report is the main-effects fit of aggregate used for the verification of @sec-basis-par. It is judged on the first three criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2, a significant model, no significant lack of fit and the limit on overfitting. PCMP-001 §7.5 names these three for a model whose bound widens a criterion, and this report applies them to the fit whose bound tightens one.

The duplicate runs at each level give the pure error of the study, the combined variability of the process and the assay, as a pooled standard deviation with `{python} PE_DF` degrees of freedom for each output. PCP-010 §5.5 takes the pure error from the replicated set-point condition. This study replicates every level, so the pure error is pooled over all of them (`{python} PD[6]`). PCP-010 §5.3 leaves to this report how its rule for small changes and the slope test are applied together. This report applies both to aggregate, the attribute whose changes the rule concerns. The slope test decides whether aggregate is affected, and the change across the range is compared with the pure error. For aggregate the two agreed for every parameter (@sec-aggregate). The acidic charge variants lie near `{python} fx(AC_MEAN, 0)` %, against a limit of quantitation of `{python} fg(ICIEF_LOQ)` % for icIEF. The rule for the low end of the method range therefore does not apply to them, and the slope test alone decides.

The buffer exchange was analysed by fitting the exponential decay that the mechanism predicts (@sec-prior), as the natural logarithm of the residual process buffer regressed on the number of diavolumes. PCP-010 §5.5 plans that fit on the conductivity series of each run. The study record holds no such series, so the fit was made across the runs of the diavolume series, on one result per run (`{python} PD[6]`). Complete passage of the buffer species through the membrane gives a slope of −1 on that scale.

Each attribute result was judged on its own against its criterion, as PCMP-001 §6.2 requires for a quality attribute and PCP-010 §7.2 states for this step. Aggregate was judged at manufacturing scale and the acidic charge variants as measured (@sec-sdm). The PAR of a parameter is the contiguous span of levels over which every attribute measured on the final retentate met its criterion, with the other parameters at their set-points (PCP-010 §8).

The study record of `{python} UNI2_ID` does not give the order in which its runs were made (`{python} PD[4]`). It cannot show the randomized order that PCP-010 §6.2 requires, and a drift over the course of the study could not be separated from a slope.

The capability of the drug substance comes from the integrated process model of PCMP-001 §6.5. The model runs `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches through every step. Each process parameter is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a standard deviation of one sixth of the width of its NOR, and the draw is clipped to the range studied. The NOR of the number of diavolumes is a minimum and has no upper edge. The model draws it around its set-point of `{python} sp_s("diavolumes")` with a standard deviation of `{python} fx(DV_SIM_SD)` DV, one sixth of a range of `{python} fg(NOR["diavolumes"][0])`–`{python} u_("diavolumes", DV_COMBO_HI)`, and never below the minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])` or above `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][1])`. The model includes the effects of the UF/DF parameters on aggregate and no effect of them on the acidic charge variants. PCMP-001 §7.9 sets a target Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and a minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)`.

# Study design {#sec-design}

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space {#sec-factors}

@tbl-factors gives the parameters with their set-points, NORs, ranges studied and the levels of `{python} UNI2_ID`. Each range studied extends beyond the NOR at one end or at both, and it is the knowledge space within which a PAR can be claimed.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_fa = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k], UNIT[k], fg(SP[k]), nor_cell(k) + ("^a)^" if ONE_SIDED[k] else ""),
                     f"{fg(RNG[k][0])}–{fg(RNG[k][1])}",
                     ", ".join(fg(v) for v in sorted(U.loc[U["parameter"] == k, "value"].unique()))]
                    for k in PK],
                   columns=["Parameter", "Unit", "Set-point", "NOR", "Range\nstudied", f"Levels of\n{UNI2_ID}"])
T.frame(_fa, "Parameters of the step: set-points, normal operating ranges, ranges studied and the levels "
             "of the univariate study.", "tbl-factors",
        align=["P{4.2cm}", "l", "r", "l", "l", "P{4.0cm}"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("a)", "A minimum. The parameter is counted to its set-point and is not run below this value.")]).show()
```

The `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` was studied over `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")`. Its NOR is a minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. The step counts diavolumes to its set-point of `{python} sp_s("diavolumes")` and is not run below the minimum. Each further diavolume lowers the residual process buffer further. It also adds passes through the pump, which could raise aggregate, and time on the skid, which could raise the acidic charge variants. The range studied therefore extends to `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][1])` to measure those effects. Across `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")` the slope of aggregate was not significant (`{python} pe(sDV["p"])`), and the 95 % confidence interval of the change runs from `{python} fx(sDV["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sDV["ch_hi"])` percentage points (@sec-aggregate). The study does not go below the minimum. TMP was studied over `{python} rng_s("tmp")` against a NOR of `{python} nor_s("tmp")`. The range extends above the NOR to measure whether a higher TMP, which raises the antibody concentration at the membrane wall or compacts the polarization layer, raises aggregate. Its lower edge is the lower edge of the NOR. A lower TMP lowers the flux and lengthens the operation, and the study does not characterize that side. The `{python} nm["final_conc"]` was studied over `{python} rng_s("final_conc")` against a NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`, on both sides. Above the target a higher final concentration raises the viscosity and the bulk concentration of the retentate, which lowers the flux and holds more of the antibody at high concentration. The range extends below the NOR as well, so that a retentate concentrated short of the target is also covered. No PAR is claimed beyond the range studied (PCMP-001 §7.6).

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

PCP-010 §6.2 planned the univariate study `{python} UNI_ID`. Each parameter was to be run at the two edges of its range studied and at its set-point, with the other two at their set-points. The set-point condition was shared by the series and replicated, and the order of execution was to be randomized across the study. The planned study ran from `{python} UNI_START` to `{python} UNI_END` on `{python} UNI_EQ`, the skid of the qualification. No result of it for any parameter effect is in the record, and Version 1.0 described its outcome without one.

The further univariate study `{python} UNI2_ID` was made from `{python} UNI2_START` to `{python} UNI2_END`, during the re-analysis and after INV-001 closed on `{python} INV["closed"]`. It gave the parameters the recorded results that Version 1.0 lacked. Each parameter was run at `{python} w(N_LEV)` levels, in duplicate, with the other two at their set-points. The low and high levels are the edges of the range studied, and the two intermediate levels lie halfway between the set-point and each edge (@tbl-factors). The study has `{python} N_RUNS2` runs, `{python} w(N_SP2)` of them at the set-point condition. It ran on `{python} UNI2_EQ`, a second UF/DF TFF skid, which was in calibration at execution, with its next calibration due on `{python} CALDUE[UNI2_EQ]`. The qualification and the planned univariate study on the first skid both closed before its next calibration, which was due on `{python} CALDUE[SDM_EQ]`.

`{python} UNI2_ID` is not a designed experiment, and no run combines the levels of two parameters. The effects, PARs and classes of this report rest on one parameter at a time. Only the verification of aggregate in @sec-basis-par fits the three parameters together, with no interaction term (`{python} PD[8]`). The study differs from the plan in its levels, its replicates and its skid (`{python} PD1`).

# Results {#sec-results}

## Reproducibility of the duplicate runs {#sec-repro}

@tbl-repro gives the pure error of each output and the results of the `{python} w(N_SP2)` set-point runs, `{python} w(N_REP)` in each series. The pure error of aggregate was `{python} fx(PE[AG][0], 3)` percentage points and that of the acidic charge variants `{python} fx(PE[AC][0])` percentage points. The pure error of the step yield was `{python} fx(PE["yield_pct"][0], 2)` percentage points, and that of the final concentration `{python} fx(PE["ds_concentration_g_per_l"][0])` g/L. The set-point runs of the `{python} w(N_P)` series gave a mean aggregate of `{python} fx(AGG_SP2_MEAN)` % with a standard deviation of `{python} fx(SP2[AG].std(ddof=1), 3)` percentage points.

## Effects of the parameters {#sec-effects}

@tbl-slopes gives, for each parameter and output, the change across the range studied that the slope predicts, its 95 % confidence interval and the p-value of the slope. Of the `{python} N_SLOPES` slopes, `{python} w(N_SIG)` were significant at α = `{python} fg(ALPHA)`. The `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` affected the residual process buffer. TMP and the final DS concentration affected aggregate, and the final DS concentration affected the final concentration achieved, which is its own setting. No slope of the acidic charge variants or of the step yield was significant, and neither TMP nor the final DS concentration had a significant slope on the residual process buffer.

```{python}

CLAB = {"aggregate_out_pct": "Aggregates, HMW (pp)", "acidic_variants": "Acidic variants (pp)",

T.frame(_sl, f"Change of each output across the range studied, from the slope of the individual results on "
             f"the setting, {UNI2_ID}.", "tbl-slopes", merge=["Parameter and\nrange studied"],
        align=["P{3.2cm}", "P{4.8cm}", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"pp, percentage points. Change across the range studied, the slope times the width of the "
```
