## Aggregate {#sec-aggregate}

Every aggregate result met the criterion of `{python} CRIT_AG` at manufacturing scale, also with the offset at the end of its interval that is least favourable to the criterion. The highest result was `{python} fx(AGG_MAX)` % HMW, `{python} where(AGG_MAX_K, AGG_MAX_V)`, and it lay `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion. @fig-agg-acidic shows the individual results against each parameter.

Aggregate rose with the final DS concentration. Across the range studied of `{python} rng_s("final_conc")` the slope predicts a rise of `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` percentage points (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(sC["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sC["ch_hi"])`, `{python} pe(sC["p"])`), and across the NOR a rise of `{python} fx(CH_C_NOR)`. Aggregate also rose with TMP, by `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points across `{python} rng_s("tmp")` (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(sT["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sT["ch_hi"])`, `{python} pe(sT["p"])`) and by `{python} fx(CH_T_NOR)` across the NOR. Both changes across the range are larger than the pure error of `{python} fx(PE[AG][0], 3)` percentage points. Under the rule of PCP-010 §5.3, a change larger than the pure error is not assay noise, so neither is attributed to the assay. Both agree in direction with the expectation of @sec-prior. The larger change, for the final DS concentration, is `{python} fx(SHARE_C, 0)` % of the margin between the highest result and the criterion. This report judges both changes small against the criterion (`{python} PD[6]`).

No effect of the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` on aggregate was detected (`{python} pe(sDV["p"])`). The 95 % confidence interval of the change across `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")` runs from `{python} fx(sDV["ch_lo"])` to `{python} fx(sDV["ch_hi"])` percentage points. More diavolumes add passes through the pump, and @sec-prior expected aggregate to rise with them. The data do not show that rise at the precision of the study, and an effect within the interval cannot be excluded.

```{python}
#| label: fig-agg-acidic
#| fig-cap: "Aggregate at manufacturing scale (upper row) and acidic charge variants as measured (lower row) in the final retentate against each parameter, S-UFDF-UNI2. Each point is one run. Aggregate at manufacturing scale is the result minus the aggregate offset. The grey band is the NOR, open to the right for the number of diavolumes, whose NOR is a minimum. A solid line is the fitted slope where the slope is significant. The dashed line is the lower limit of the criterion for the acidic charge variants. The aggregate criterion lies far above the plotted range."
#| fig-width: 7.2
#| fig-height: 4.9
_fig, _ax = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(7.2, 4.9))
_ylim_ag = (U["agg_mfg"].min() - 0.03, U["agg_mfg"].max() + 0.03)
_off_ag = OFF[AG]["offset"]
_ylim_ac = (AC_LO - 0.8, U[AC].max() + 0.8)
for _j, k in enumerate(PK):
    _g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    _pad = 0.05 * (RNG[k][1] - RNG[k][0])
    for _r_i, (r, col, lab, yl, sh) in enumerate([(AG, "agg_mfg", "Aggregates, HMW,\nMfg scale (%)", _ylim_ag, _off_ag),
                                                   (AC, AC, "Acidic variants (%)", _ylim_ac, 0.0)]):
        a = _ax[_r_i, _j]
        a.axvspan(NOR[k][0], RNG[k][1] + _pad if ONE_SIDED[k] else NOR[k][1], color="0.9", lw=0, zorder=0)
        a.plot(_g["value"], _g[col], "o", ms=4, color="#1f5f8b", zorder=3)
        if (k, r) in SIG:
            _xs = np.array(RNG[k])
            a.plot(_xs, SL[(k, r)]["ic"] - sh + SL[(k, r)]["slope"] * _xs, "-", color="#b5562b", lw=1.4, zorder=2)
        if r == AC:
            a.axhline(AC_LO, ls="--", color="#b5562b", lw=1)
        a.set_xlim(RNG[k][0] - _pad, RNG[k][1] + _pad)
        a.set_ylim(*yl)
        a.tick_params(labelsize=8)
        if _r_i == 1:
            a.set_xlabel(f"{NAME[k]} ({UNIT[k]})", fontsize=9)
        if _j == 0:
            a.set_ylabel(lab, fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Acidic charge variants {#sec-acidic}

Every result of the acidic charge variants lay within the criterion of `{python} CRIT_AC`, at both ends. The lowest result, `{python} fx(AC_MIN, 1)` %, was measured `{python} "twice" if len(AC_MIN_TIES) == 2 else w(len(AC_MIN_TIES)) + " times"`, `{python} " and ".join(where(_r.parameter, _r.value) for _r in AC_MIN_TIES.itertuples())`. It lay `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_LO, 1)` percentage points above the lower limit. The highest was `{python} fx(AC_MAX, 1)` %, `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_HI, 1)` percentage points below the upper limit. No slope was significant (`{python} pe(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["p"])`, `{python} pe(SL[("tmp", AC)]["p"])` and `{python} pe(SL[("final_conc", AC)]["p"])` for the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, TMP and the final DS concentration). The 95 % confidence intervals of the change across the range studied run from `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["ch_hi"], 1)`, from `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", AC)]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", AC)]["ch_hi"], 1)` and from `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", AC)]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", AC)]["ch_hi"], 1)` percentage points, in the same order. A change of up to `{python} fx(AC_CH_BOUND, 1)` percentage points across a range therefore cannot be excluded. @sec-prior expected deamidation to raise the acidic charge variants with the number of diavolumes and the final DS concentration, which lengthen the operation, and to lower them with TMP, which shortens it.

The acidic charge variants enter the step with the load from the virus filtration step. They are formed first in the production bioreactor, whose report PCR-003 characterizes them, and deamidation adds to them wherever the antibody is held in solution. Without a load result the study cannot say how much the step adds at the set-point condition (@sec-sampling). Deamidation can only raise the acidic charge variants, so whatever the step adds moves them toward the upper limit of `{python} fg(AC_HI)` % and away from the lower limit of `{python} fg(AC_LO)` %.

## Buffer exchange {#sec-buffer}

The residual process buffer fell exponentially with the number of diavolumes (@fig-buffer). The slope of its natural logarithm on the number of diavolumes was `{python} fx(RB_B, 3)` (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(RB_LO, 3)` to `{python} fx(RB_HI, 3)`, R² = `{python} fx(RB_R2, 3)`). The interval includes −1, the slope that complete passage of the buffer species through the membrane gives. Each diavolume removed `{python} fx(RB_REMOVED, 0)` % of the process buffer that remained, and the residual fell by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` per diavolume. The two runs at the set-point of `{python} sp_s("diavolumes")` in the diavolume series gave a mean residual of `{python} fx(RB_SP["mean"], 3)` % of the process buffer. At the minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])` the two results were `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["min"], 3)` and `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` %. At the top of the range studied, `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][1])`, neither result exceeded `{python} fx(RB_TOP["max"], 4)` %. The residual process buffer had no significant slope on TMP (`{python} pe(SL[("tmp", "residual_buffer_pct")]["p"])`) or on the final DS concentration (`{python} pe(SL[("final_conc", "residual_buffer_pct")]["p"])`), as a wash-out that depends on the number of diavolumes alone would predict.

```{python}
#| label: fig-buffer
#| fig-cap: "Residual process buffer in the final retentate against the number of diavolumes, S-UFDF-UNI2, on a logarithmic scale. Each point is one run. The line is the exponential fall fitted to the runs of the series. On this scale an exponential fall is a straight line, and a levelling off would show as a bend. The grey band is the NOR, a minimum, open to the right."
#| fig-width: 5.4
#| fig-height: 3.4
_fig, a = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.4, 3.4))
_padb = 0.05 * (RNG["diavolumes"][1] - RNG["diavolumes"][0])
a.axvspan(NOR["diavolumes"][0], RNG["diavolumes"][1] + _padb, color="0.9", lw=0, zorder=0)
a.semilogy(G["value"], G["residual_buffer_pct"], "o", ms=5, color="#1f5f8b", zorder=3)
_xs = np.linspace(RNG["diavolumes"][0], RNG["diavolumes"][1], 50)
a.semilogy(_xs, np.exp(RB_IC + RB_B * _xs), "-", color="#b5562b", lw=1.4, zorder=2)
a.set_xlim(RNG["diavolumes"][0] - _padb, RNG["diavolumes"][1] + _padb)
a.set_xlabel(f"{NAME['diavolumes']} ({UNIT['diavolumes']})", fontsize=9)
a.set_ylabel("Residual process buffer (%)", fontsize=9)
a.tick_params(labelsize=8)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The two results at each level of the diavolume series lay wholly above both results at the next level, at every step from `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][0])` to `{python} u_("diavolumes", RNG["diavolumes"][1])`.

PCP-010 judges the buffer exchange on the conductivity of the retentate. Section 5.5 of the plan places the end of the exchange at the number of diavolumes at which "the conductivity of the retentate has reached the plateau set by the formulation buffer and no further change is measured over the following diavolume". Section 7.2 accepts the buffer exchange when the conductivity and the pH have reached that plateau at or below `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. The study record holds no conductivity or pH reading (`{python} PD[2]`), so the criterion could not be judged as planned. The residual process buffer cannot stand in for the conductivity. It falls by a constant fraction with each diavolume, so it does not level off within any range that an assay can resolve.

The buffer exchange is controlled instead by its minimum number of diavolumes, `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`, the lower edge of a one-sided NOR. The formulation buffer of the drug substance is confirmed against its release limits (`{python} PD[7]`). The result of this study is the residual process buffer at each number of diavolumes, at most `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` % of the process buffer at the minimum.

Objective (iii), to establish the number of diavolumes at which the retentate reaches the formulation buffer, is not met. The study gives the residual process buffer after each number of diavolumes, but not that number.

## Step yield and final concentration {#sec-yield}

The step yield ranged from `{python} fx(Y_MIN, 1)` to `{python} fx(Y_MAX, 1)` %, with a mean of `{python} fx(Y_MEAN, 1)` %. No slope of the step yield was significant. The 95 % confidence intervals of its change across the range studied run from `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", "yield_pct")]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("diavolumes", "yield_pct")]["ch_hi"], 1)` percentage points for the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]`, from `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", "yield_pct")]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("tmp", "yield_pct")]["ch_hi"], 1)` for TMP and from `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", "yield_pct")]["ch_lo"], 1)` to `{python} fx(SL[("final_conc", "yield_pct")]["ch_hi"], 1)` for the final DS concentration. The step yield has no criterion and is reported for information.

The final concentration followed its setting in the series of the final DS concentration, with a slope of `{python} fx(sFC["slope"], 3)` (95 % confidence interval `{python} fx(sFC["lo"], 3)` to `{python} fx(sFC["hi"], 3)`). Each result lay within `{python} fx(FC_DIFF_MAX, 1)` g/L of its setting. In the other two series, run at the target of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")`, the final concentration ranged from `{python} fx(FC_OTH.min(), 1)` to `{python} fx(FC_OTH.max(), 1)` g/L, inside the NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`. The pure error of the final concentration, `{python} fx(PE["ds_concentration_g_per_l"][0])` g/L, compares with a precision of the A280 method of `{python} fg(A280_PREC)` %, which is `{python} fx(A280_SD_AT_TARGET, 1)` g/L at the target.

## Mechanistic interpretation {#sec-mechanism}

The rise of aggregate with the final DS concentration and with TMP is consistent with aggregate forming in the polarization layer at the membrane wall. The final DS concentration raises the bulk concentration at the end of the operation, and below the limiting flux it raises the concentration at the wall too. Below the limiting flux TMP raises the concentration at the wall by driving more permeate through the membrane. Above it, the concentration at the wall stays at its limiting value, and a higher TMP compacts and thickens the layer, so more antibody is held at that concentration. The study did not measure the flux across the TMP range, so it cannot say on which side of the limiting flux the set-point lies. Within the NOR the two effects amount to `{python} fx(CH_C_NOR)` and `{python} fx(CH_T_NOR)` percentage points.

No effect of the number of diavolumes on aggregate was detected, although more diavolumes add passes through the pump. Diafiltration is made before the second concentration, at a lower antibody concentration than the final one. If aggregate forms mainly where the concentration at the wall is highest, extra diavolumes at that lower concentration would add little. The study did not measure where in the step aggregate forms, so this explanation is not tested.

The acidic charge variants did not change detectably over the ranges studied, although each parameter changes the time the antibody spends in solution. The study record does not give the duration of the runs, so the study cannot relate the acidic charge variants to the time in solution. Any deamidation in the step would raise them, toward the upper limit of the criterion.

The fall of the residual process buffer by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume is consistent with free passage of the buffer species through the membrane, which diafiltration at constant volume relies on. The study did not measure the pH or the excipient levels of the final retentate. It therefore gives no evidence on the Donnan and volume-exclusion effects that can move them away from the values of the buffer at high concentration.

# Design space {#sec-design-space}

No design space is defined for UF/DF. A design space is a multivariate region [@ichq8]. A study that varies one parameter at a time cannot define one, because it gives no result where two parameters are away from their set-points at the same time. The step is described instead by the univariate PAR of each parameter, which equals its range studied (@sec-pars). These data support the movement of one parameter within its PAR, with the others at their set-points. @sec-par-table gives only the size that an interaction would need to bring aggregate to its criterion. An excursion outside a NOR in manufacture is dispositioned against the PAR (PCP-010 §8). A planned move of an operating range is a change, and it is assessed under change management before it is made [@ichq10].

# Proven acceptable ranges {#sec-pars}

## Acceptance basis {#sec-basis-par}

No step follows UF/DF, so PCMP-001 Table 7.1 defines no IAC for it, and the drug substance criteria apply directly (PCMP-001 §7.6). Aggregate must not exceed `{python} fg(AG_HI)` % HMW, and the acidic charge variants must lie between `{python} fg(AC_LO)` and `{python} fg(AC_HI)` %. Both criteria come from the drug substance CQA register (PCMP-001 §3), and no result of these studies enters them.

The a priori derivation of the criteria upstream of this step assumes that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and that no step after low-pH viral inactivation changes the acidic charge variants (PCMP-001 §7.3). On that assumption the cation exchange pool carried the drug substance criterion for aggregate itself, `{python} fx(AG_HI)` % HMW. This study shows that two parameters of UF/DF raise aggregate within their NORs. On the sum of the two slopes the rise at the corner of `{python} u_("final_conc", NOR["final_conc"][1])` and `{python} u_("tmp", NOR["tmp"][1])` is `{python} fx(ADD_NOR)` percentage points above the level at the set-point.

This report checks the assumption of no aggregate change after cation exchange on the results of `{python} UNI2_ID`, as PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.5 states. PCP-010 §7.2 planned no verification at this step (`{python} PD[8]`). The aggregate results, with the aggregate offset subtracted, are fitted to the main effects of the `{python} w(N_P)` parameters, with all runs pooled and no interaction term. The fit is evaluated at every combination of NOR low, set-point and NOR high, as for a step with a response-surface model. For the number of diavolumes, whose NOR is a minimum, the upper value of the combinations is `{python} u_("diavolumes", DV_COMBO_HI)`, the value that also sets the spread of the simulation (@sec-stats). At the least favourable combination the fit predicts a mean rise of `{python} fx(UF_WORST_MEAN, 3)` percentage points above its value at the set-point. The one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single run puts the rise at `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points. The fit meets the first three criteria of PCMP-001 §7.2. The model is significant (`{python} pe(UF_PF)`), it has no significant lack of fit (`{python} pe(UF_PLOF)`), and R² exceeds predicted R² by `{python} fx(UF_GAP)`, within the limit of `{python} fg(THRESHOLDS["max_r2_minus_pred_r2"])`. PCMP-001 §7.5 rule 1 states that where the worst case predicted within the NOR is worse than the platform worst case, the prediction bound of a single batch replaces the platform value. Here the bound replaces the assumption of no change, and every aggregate criterion upstream carries it. The criterion of the cation exchange pool is tightened from `{python} fx(AG_HI)` to `{python} fx(CEX_AG)` % HMW, and the cation exchange report PCR-007 judges its pool against that value. The fit assumes that the parameters act independently, and @sec-par-table gives the size that an interaction would need to matter.

For the acidic charge variants no slope was significant. The change across the step was not measured, because no load was sampled (`{python} PD[3]`), and a rise of up to `{python} fx(AC_CH_BOUND, 1)` percentage points across a range cannot be excluded (@sec-acidic). The assumption of PCMP-001 §7.3 that no step after low-pH viral inactivation changes the acidic charge variants ignores the deamidation on the UF/DF skid, which raises them (@sec-prior). Deamidation moves the acidic charge variants away from the lower limit of `{python} fg(AC_LO)` %, which is the limiting side (@sec-capability), so the assumption errs on the safe side for that limit. Toward the upper limit of `{python} fg(AC_HI)` %, every result of this study lay at least `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_HI, 1)` percentage points inside.

## Results against the criteria {#sec-criteria}

@tbl-levels gives, for each level of each parameter, the lowest and highest aggregate result at manufacturing scale and the lowest and highest result of the acidic charge variants. PCP-010 §7.3 accepts a level when every attribute measured on the final retentate of its runs meets its criterion. Every attribute result of every level met its criterion, so every level is acceptable. The plan passes a parameter over its range when every level is acceptable and the change measured across the range is small against the criterion. It leaves the threshold for a small change to this report (`{python} PD[6]`). This report gives the changes (@tbl-slopes) and the margins (@tbl-levels) and judges each change small against its criterion. The largest significant change of an attribute across a range, `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` percentage points of aggregate for the final DS concentration, is `{python} fx(SHARE_C_CRIT, 1)` % of the criterion of `{python} fg(AG_HI)` % HMW. The acidic charge variants have no significant change. A change of up to `{python} fx(AC_CH_BOUND, 1)` percentage points across a range cannot be excluded, and that is smaller than the margin of `{python} fx(AC_MARGIN_LO, 1)` percentage points between the lowest result and the lower limit. No level failed, so the rules for a failing level were not used, and the study record shows no repeated run.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_lv = []
for k in PK:
    _g = U[U["parameter"] == k]
    for lvl in LEVELS:
        _h = _g[_g["level"] == lvl]
        _v = float(_h["value"].iloc[0])
        _ok = bool((_h["agg_mfg"] <= AG_HI).all() and _h[AC].between(AC_LO, AC_HI).all())
        assert _ok
        _in = (NOR[k][0] <= _v) if ONE_SIDED[k] else (NOR[k][0] <= _v <= NOR[k][1])
        _lv.append([f"{NAME[k]} ({UNIT[k]})", Cap(lvl), fg(_v), "Yes" if _in else "No",
                    span(_h["agg_mfg"].min(), _h["agg_mfg"].max(), 2), span(_h[AC].min(), _h[AC].max(), 1)])
_lv = pd.DataFrame(_lv, columns=["Parameter", "Level", "Setting", "Inside\nthe NOR",
                                 "Aggregates, HMW,\nMfg scale (%)", "Acidic\nvariants (%)"])
T.frame(_lv, f"Lowest and highest result of each level, {UNI2_ID}. Every result met its criterion.", "tbl-levels",
        merge=["Parameter"], align=["P{3.4cm}", "l", "r", "c", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"The criteria are {CRIT_AG} for aggregate and {CRIT_AC} for the acidic variants. Aggregate "
                    "at manufacturing scale, the scale-down result minus the aggregate offset. Acidic variants as "
                    f"measured. Each level has {N_REP} runs, and a single value means that both gave it at the "
                    "precision shown. The NOR of the number of diavolumes is a minimum.")]).show()
```

## Proven acceptable ranges of the parameters {#sec-par-table}

@tbl-pars gives the PAR of each parameter. Each PAR rests on aggregate and the acidic charge variants, the attributes the study measured, and on no other attribute. For the final DS concentration the PAR extends `{python} u_("final_conc", MARG["final_conc"][0])` beyond the NOR at each end. For TMP it extends `{python} u_("tmp", MARG["tmp"][1])` above the NOR, and its lower edge is the lower edge of the NOR. The NOR of the `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` is a minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`, and the PAR starts at that minimum. The PAR ends at `{python} u_("diavolumes", PARS["diavolumes"][1])`, because the study gives no result above it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_pa = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k], nor_s(k) + ("^a)^" if ONE_SIDED[k] else ""),
                     f"{fg(PARS[k][0])}–{fg(PARS[k][1])} {UNIT[k]}",
                     marg_s(k, 0), marg_s(k, 1)] for k in PK],
                   columns=["Parameter", "NOR", "PAR", "PAR beyond\nthe NOR, low", "PAR beyond\nthe NOR, high"])
T.frame(_pa, "Proven acceptable ranges of the parameters, with the other parameters at their set-points.",
        "tbl-pars", align=["P{4.2cm}", "l", "l", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "Each PAR is the range studied. It rests on aggregate and the acidic charge variants, the "
                    "attributes measured in the final retentate."),
               ("a)", "A minimum. The parameter is counted to its set-point and is not run below this value.")]).show()
```

Three limitations apply to these PARs, as PCP-010 §8 states them.

1. Each PAR holds with the other parameters at their set-points. It does not describe the step when two parameters sit at their range edges at the same time.
2. PCMP-001 §6.4 defines a second analysis, which predicts each attribute from a fitted model while the other parameters are drawn at random around their set-points. This step has no such model, so that analysis was not performed. For a parameter studied one factor at a time the range rests on its own data instead (PCMP-001 §4).
3. A PAR cannot be wider than the range studied. Each PAR here is the range studied, and no claim is made beyond it (PCMP-001 §7.6).

PCP-010 §4.3 asks for runs with two parameters at their range edges together where a measured attribute approaches its criterion at an edge. It leaves the threshold for "approaches" to this report (`{python} PD[6]`). At every edge the highest aggregate result lay at least `{python} fx(EDGE_AG_MARGIN)` percentage points below its criterion, and the acidic charge variants lay at least `{python} fx(EDGE_AC_MARGIN, 1)` percentage points inside theirs. This report judges that no attribute approached its criterion at an edge, and no such runs were made.

The interaction of TMP and the final DS concentration that @sec-risk describes was not measured. Its possible size can be set against the criterion for a single run. The highest set-point run gave `{python} fx(SP_AGG_MFG_MAX)` % HMW at manufacturing scale. At the corner of the ranges studied, `{python} u_("final_conc", RNG["final_conc"][1])` and `{python} u_("tmp", RNG["tmp"][1])`, the two slopes add `{python} fx(ADD_RNG)` percentage points to give `{python} fx(PRED_RNG)` % HMW. An interaction would have to add a further `{python} fx(GAP_RNG)` percentage points there, about `{python} fx(RATIO_RNG, 0)` times the rise that the two slopes give, to bring that run to the criterion. The study cannot exclude an interaction, but one of that size is far outside the effects it measured.

# Process capability and robustness {#sec-capability}

UF/DF delivers the drug substance, so this report gives the capability of the drug substance for the attributes that the step can change and for residual DNA. @tbl-capability gives the result of the integrated process model for `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches, with each process parameter drawn as @sec-stats describes (PCMP-001 §6.5). The model includes an effect of the final DS concentration and of TMP on aggregate. The table gives each Cpk, the count of simulated batches outside the criterion and the tail probability of a normal distribution with the simulated mean and standard deviation. PCMP-001 §7.9 sets a target Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_TARGET)` and a minimum of `{python} fx(CPK_MIN)`.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_crit = cqas_by_keys(["aggregates_hmw", "acidic_variants", "residual_dna"])["Acceptance"].tolist()
_cp = []
def sig3(x):
    """Three significant figures, written out without an exponent."""
    d = max(0, 2 - int(np.floor(np.log10(abs(x)))))
    return fx(x, d)
for _n, (k, dm, ds) in enumerate([("aggregates_hmw", 2, 3), ("acidic_variants", 1, 2), ("residual_dna", None, None)]):
    _c = float(CAPT.loc[k, "Cpk"])
    _m = sig3(MCS[k][0]) if dm is None else fx(MCS[k][0], dm)
    _sd = sig3(MCS[k][1]) if ds is None else fx(MCS[k][1], ds)
    _cp.append([CAPT.loc[k, "cqa"], _crit[_n], _m, _sd, fx(_c, 2),
                str(NOOS[k]), "< 0.001" if PPM[k] < 0.001 else fx(PPM[k], 0)])
_cp = pd.DataFrame(_cp, columns=["CQA", "Criterion", "Mean", "SD", "Cpk",
                                 f"Simulated batches\noutside, of {N_MC_S}", "Normal tail,\nper million batches"])
T.frame(_cp, "Capability of the drug substance in the integrated process model.", "tbl-capability",
        align=["P{3.4cm}", "P{2.6cm}", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"], size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", f"Mean and SD of the simulated batches. Residual DNA in ng per dose, for a dose of "
                    f"{fg(DOSE_MG)} mg of antibody. Normal tail, the probability beyond the criterion of a normal "
                    "distribution with the simulated mean and SD, two-sided for a two-sided criterion.")]).show()
```

Aggregate has a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)`, above the target, and no simulated batch lay outside its criterion. The mean simulated aggregate is `{python} fx(MCS["aggregates_hmw"][0])` % HMW, with a standard deviation of `{python} fx(MCS["aggregates_hmw"][1], 3)` percentage points. A Cpk this large says only that the criterion lies far beyond the simulated batches. Aggregate is therefore judged on the individual results of the study (@sec-criteria) and on the count of simulated batches outside the criterion. With none of `{python} N_MC_S` outside, the one-sided 95 % upper confidence bound of the probability of a batch outside is `{python} fx(P_UB_PCT, 2)` %. That bound covers the sampling of the simulation and not the uncertainty of the integrated process model.

The acidic charge variants have a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AC)` in the integrated process model, between the minimum and the target. The Cpk is set by the distance from the simulated mean to the lower limit of the criterion, `{python} fg(AC_LO)` %. Of the `{python} N_MC_S` simulated batches, `{python} w(NOOS["acidic_variants"])` fell outside the criterion, and the normal tail probability is `{python} fx(PPM["acidic_variants"], 0)` per million. This step does not move the acidic charge variants toward that lower limit. Deamidation can only raise them, and the integrated process model gives the UF/DF parameters no effect on them. The attribute is formed in the production bioreactor, and its report PCR-003 gives the parameters that drive it and the controls that address them.

The results of this study do not confirm the simulated level. All `{python} N_RUNS2` results of `{python} UNI2_ID` lay between `{python} fx(AC_MIN, 1)` and `{python} fx(AC_MAX, 1)` %, below the simulated mean of `{python} fx(AC_SIM_MEAN, 1)` %. Their level is the level of the load, which was not sampled (`{python} PD[3]`). At the mean of the study, `{python} fx(AC_MEAN, 1)` %, with the simulated standard deviation, the Cpk would be `{python} fx(CPK_AC_MEAS)`, below the minimum. The capability of the acidic charge variants therefore depends on the level that the upstream steps deliver, and this report cannot settle it from its own results. PCMR-001 assesses it across the whole process.

Residual DNA is judged in ng per dose, the unit of its criterion of `{python} fg(DNA_CRIT)` ng per dose. That criterion is the acceptable range that the A-Mab case study claims for residual DNA [@amab2009, Table 2.17, pp. 47–48]. The dose is A-Mab's `{python} fg(DOSE["mg_per_kg"])` mg/kg [@amab2009, p. 26] for a body weight of `{python} fg(DOSE["body_weight_kg"])` kg. The body weight is an assumption of this campaign, and with it a dose carries `{python} fg(DOSE_MG)` mg of antibody. The simulated drug substance carries a mean of `{python} fx(DNA_MEAN, 5)` ng per dose, or `{python} fx(DNA_PG, 5)` pg per mg of antibody, with a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_DNA, 1)`. No simulated batch lay outside the criterion, and the same upper bound of `{python} fx(P_UB_PCT, 2)` % applies. This level is not a measured result. It is computed from the DNA clearance that the integrated process model credits to each purification step, which is an input from outside the data of this step. It lies about `{python} DNA_LOQ_RATIO_S` times below the limit of quantitation of the qPCR method for residual DNA, `{python} fg(DNA_LOQ)` pg per mg (AMV-3014), so that method could not quantify it. The reports of the capture and polishing steps (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008) give the DNA results of their studies. Residual DNA has no IAC, because the platform history gives no worst-case DNA clearance for the steps after Protein A, so no criterion can be carried back (PCMP-001 §7.3). Platform experience shows that DNA is consistently cleared from the process [@amab2009, p. 47]. In the testing plan of the A-Mab case study an attribute of low criticality with moderate to high process capability would likely not require testing [@amab2009, p. 57]. No DNA clearance is credited to UF/DF.

# Parameter classification {#sec-classification}

The parameters were classified under SOP-4001 by the rules of PCMP-001 §7.7, which follow the decision logic of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009]. A critical process parameter (CPP) has "an effect on a CQA that is significant and practically relevant within the characterized range, and a high risk of falling outside its acceptable range in operation". A well-controlled critical process parameter has the same kind of effect but a low risk, because it is readily controlled and its PAR is wide against its NOR. A KPP "affects process performance, such as yield or concentration, and has no effect on a CQA within its range". PCMP-001 §7.7 adds that "a significant effect that is too small to move the attribute appreciably within the PAR does not by itself make a parameter critical". A significant effect on a CQA therefore makes a parameter critical unless the effect is too small to be practically relevant, and PCMP-001 and SOP-4001 set no threshold for that. Each class below is stated with the size of each effect across the PAR and the margin of the PAR to the NOR (PCP-010 §7.4). @tbl-classification summarises the evidence.

```{python}
#| output: asis
_perf = {"diavolumes": "Residual process buffer, measured",
         "tmp": "Permeate flux, from the mechanism. Not measured across the range",
         "final_conc": "Final concentration, measured"}
_cl = pd.DataFrame([[NAME[k], CLS[k],
                     f"{fx(SL[(k, AG)]['ch'])} ({fx(SL[(k, AG)]['ch_lo'])} to {fx(SL[(k, AG)]['ch_hi'])})",
                     pv(SL[(k, AG)]["p"]), pv(SL[(k, AC)]["p"]),
                     _perf[k], f"{marg_s(k, 0)} / {marg_s(k, 1)}"] for k in PK],
                   columns=["Parameter", "Class", "Change of aggregate\nacross the PAR (pp)", "p,\naggregate",
                            "p, acidic\nvariants", "Process performance\noutput", "PAR beyond the\nNOR, low / high"])
T.frame(_cl, "Evidence for the classification of the parameters.",
        "tbl-classification", align=["P{2.6cm}", "c", "r", "r", "r", "P{3.2cm}", "l"],
        size="footnotesize",
        notes=[("", "pp, percentage points of HMW. Change, the slope times the width of the PAR, with its 95 % "
                    "confidence interval in brackets. p, of the slope of the attribute on the parameter. n.a., not "
                    "applicable, because the NOR of the number of diavolumes is a minimum.")]).show()
```

- The `{python} nm["diavolumes"]` was classified as a KPP. More diavolumes lower the residual process buffer, by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume (@sec-buffer). Its slopes on aggregate (`{python} pe(sDV["p"])`) and on the acidic charge variants (`{python} pe(SL[("diavolumes", AC)]["p"])`) were not significant, so no effect on either attribute was detected within the range studied, at the precision of the duplicates. Its NOR is a minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`, and its PAR runs from that minimum to `{python} u_("diavolumes", PARS["diavolumes"][1])`.
- TMP was classified as a KPP. It has a significant effect on aggregate, a CQA (`{python} pe(sT["p"])`). Across its NOR of `{python} nor_s("tmp")` the slope raises aggregate by `{python} fx(CH_T_NOR)` percentage points, and across its PAR of `{python} rng_s("tmp")` by `{python} fx(sT["ch"])`. The highest aggregate result of the study lay `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points below the criterion. This report judges an effect of that size too small to be practically relevant, and the KPP class of both TMP and the final DS concentration rests on that judgement. The effect is carried into product quality all the same, because the prediction bound of `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points that sets the criterion of the cation exchange pool includes it (@sec-basis-par). The effect of TMP on process performance, through the permeate flux and so the duration of the operation, was not measured across the TMP range (@tbl-classification). The flux was measured only at the set-point, in `{python} SDM_ID`. The PAR extends `{python} u_("tmp", MARG["tmp"][1])` above the NOR and not below it.
- The final DS concentration was classified as a KPP. It sets the concentration of the drug substance, which followed it with a slope of `{python} fx(sFC["slope"], 3)` (@sec-yield). It has a significant effect on aggregate, a CQA (`{python} pe(sC["p"])`). Across its NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")` the slope raises aggregate by `{python} fx(CH_C_NOR)` percentage points, and across its PAR of `{python} rng_s("final_conc")` by `{python} fx(sC["ch"])`, against the same margin of `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points. The bound of `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points behind the criterion of the cation exchange pool includes this effect too. The PAR extends `{python} u_("final_conc", MARG["final_conc"][0])` beyond the NOR at each end.

The step has no CPP and no well-controlled CPP. Its `{python} w(N_P)` parameters are KPPs, which are controlled within their NORs so that the step performs consistently [@amab2009].

# Contribution to the control strategy {#sec-control}

The control strategy for the drug substance process is consolidated in PCMR-001. This report contributes the following.

1. The NORs of the parameters are `{python} nor_s("diavolumes")`, `{python} nor_s("tmp")` and `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`. The parameters are KPPs, and their PARs are the ranges studied. The NOR of TMP and of the final DS concentration lies inside its PAR. The NOR of the number of diavolumes is a minimum, and the PAR covers counts up to `{python} u_("diavolumes", PARS["diavolumes"][1])`. The parameters are controlled within their NORs so that the step delivers the drug substance consistently at its target concentration, with the residual process buffer that @sec-buffer gives.
2. A higher final DS concentration and a higher TMP raise aggregate, through their action on the polarization layer at the membrane wall. Within their NORs the rise is at most `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points at the prediction bound of a single run, and the criterion of the cation exchange pool carries that bound (@sec-basis-par). In the studies TMP was monitored in process and the final concentration was checked by A280, and these two checks detected the study events DEV-010-01 and DEV-010-02 (@sec-events).
3. The buffer exchange is controlled by its minimum number of diavolumes, `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. At the minimum the residual process buffer was at most `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` % of the process buffer. The formulation buffer of the drug substance is confirmed against its release limits (`{python} PD[7]`).
4. The membrane chemistry and the membrane supplier are part of the qualified state of the step, and a change to either requires a new risk assessment before these data are applied (PCP-010 §12). The composition of the formulation buffer is fixed by the drug product program, and a change to it would change the target of the buffer exchange.

Other attributes of the drug substance are controlled at other steps. The glycan variants and the acidic charge variants are formed in the production bioreactor (PCR-003). Fragments form by proteolytic clipping in culture and during the harvest hold (PCR-003, PCR-004), and slowly by hydrolysis of the hinge region in solution, and they are tested at release. Host cell protein and residual DNA are cleared by the chromatography steps (PCR-005, PCR-007 and PCR-008). Leached Protein A enters the process at capture (PCR-005) and is cleared by the polishing steps. Viral clearance is credited to low-pH viral inactivation, anion exchange and virus filtration (PCR-006, PCR-008 and PCR-009), and the cumulative claim is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Discussion {#sec-discussion}

Two parameters of UF/DF, the final DS concentration and TMP, raise aggregate. Both rises exceed the pure error of the study, and this report judges them small against the criterion. They still matter upstream. PCMP-001 had assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and the bound for a single run of `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points now tightens the criterion of the cation exchange pool to `{python} fx(CEX_AG)` % HMW. More diavolumes lower the residual process buffer, by the factor that free passage of the buffer species predicts. No slope of the acidic charge variants was significant. Every result met the drug substance criteria, and each parameter has a PAR equal to its range studied.

The scale-down model is qualified for aggregate under the approach of @sec-sdm, which judges the aggregate results with the offset at its estimate and at either end of its interval. Three points limit that confidence. The offsets were measured on the first skid, and the study ran on the second. The discrepancy entry for the use of the offsets of the first skid on the second (`{python} PD1`) accepts it because the skids share their design and their membrane and the offsets are small against the criteria. The acidic charge variants and the residual process buffer were not compared at both scales, so their representativeness rests on the kinetics of deamidation and on the passage of the buffer species through the membrane. The qualification record does not name the manufacturing-scale batches (`{python} PD[5]`). The highest aggregate result lies far below its criterion (@sec-criteria), so none of these points changes a conclusion about aggregate.

The study record of `{python} UNI2_ID` is incomplete against the plan in ways that bear on its reading. No load was sampled, so the change across the step is unknown and the study measures only how the parameters change the final retentate (`{python} PD[3]`). No conductivity or pH was read, so the buffer-exchange criterion could not be judged as planned (`{python} PD[2]`), and the buffer exchange rests on the minimum number of diavolumes and on the release of the drug substance (`{python} PD[7]`). The order of the runs and the load pool are not recorded, so a drift over the study cannot be separated from a slope (`{python} PD[4]`).

The main scientific limitation is the univariate design, which cannot measure an interaction. TMP and the final DS concentration both act on the polarization layer at the membrane wall, so an interaction between them would raise aggregate most where both are high. The prediction bound of the aggregate rise in @sec-basis-par assumes no interaction, and @sec-par-table sets the size that one would need against the criterion. Each slope rests on `{python} SLDF` degrees of freedom, so an effect smaller than the confidence intervals of @tbl-slopes may have gone undetected, for the acidic charge variants in particular.

The capability of the acidic charge variants rests on the level that the upstream steps deliver. Every result of this study lies below the mean of the integrated process model, and @sec-capability shows that the Cpk at the level of the study would fall below the minimum. PCMR-001 assesses this attribute across the whole process.

The receiving site will run the process performance qualification (PPQ) batches of the transfer protocol PTP-001 against the ranges and classes of this report (PCMP-001 §2).

# Conclusions {#sec-conclusions}

1. The bench-scale TFF model is qualified for aggregate under the approach of @sec-sdm. Its offsets from manufacturing scale were applied to the results of the second skid. The discrepancy entry for that use (`{python} PD1`) accepts it because the skids share their design and their membrane and the offsets are small against the criteria (objective i).
2. Aggregate rises with the final DS concentration and with TMP, by `{python} fx(sC["ch"])` and `{python} fx(sT["ch"])` percentage points across the ranges studied. No effect of the number of diavolumes on aggregate was detected, and no slope of the acidic charge variants was significant (objective ii). The rise across the NORs tightens the criterion of the cation exchange pool to `{python} fx(CEX_AG)` % HMW.
3. The residual process buffer falls by a factor of `{python} fx(RB_FOLD)` for each diavolume and is at most `{python} fx(RB_NORLO["max"], 3)` % of the process buffer at the minimum of `{python} u_("diavolumes", NOR["diavolumes"][0])`. The buffer-exchange criterion of PCP-010 could not be judged as planned. The buffer exchange is controlled by the minimum number of diavolumes and by the release of the drug substance against the limits of its formulation buffer. Objective (iii) is not met, because the number of diavolumes at which the retentate reaches the formulation buffer was not established.
4. Every result met the drug substance criteria for aggregate and the acidic charge variants. The PARs are `{python} rng_s("diavolumes")`, `{python} rng_s("tmp")` and `{python} rng_s("final_conc")`, each equal to its range studied (objective iv).
5. The `{python} w(N_P)` parameters are KPPs, and the step has no CPP. TMP and the final DS concentration raise aggregate by `{python} fx(CH_T_NOR)` and `{python} fx(CH_C_NOR)` percentage points across their NORs, against a margin of `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN)` percentage points to the criterion, and their KPP class rests on the size of these effects. The drug substance has a Cpk of `{python} fx(CPK_AG, 1)` for aggregate, `{python} fx(CPK_AC)` for the acidic charge variants and `{python} fx(CPK_DNA, 1)` for residual DNA in the integrated process model. The Cpk of the acidic charge variants lies between the minimum and the target of PCMP-001. At the mean of this study it would be `{python} fx(CPK_AC_MEAS)`, so it depends on the level that the upstream steps deliver (objective v).
6. Neither study event changes a conclusion. The departures from the plan are recorded as `{python} w(N_PD)` discrepancies (@sec-discrepancies). The results roll up into PCMR-001.

# Study events and discrepancies from the plan {#sec-record}

A process characterization study is not GMP manufacture and raises no deviation. PCP-010 §13 keeps the wording of Version 1.0, which records a departure from the plan during execution as a deviation. This report records two kinds of entry instead. The study events are the events of execution that Version 1.0 recorded, under the numbers that Version 1.0 gave them. The discrepancies from the plan are the departures from PCP-010, both work that the plan did not foresee and requirements of the plan that were not met.

## Study events {#sec-events}

Version 1.0 recorded `{python} w(len(EVS))` study events at this step, which @tbl-events lists.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(dev_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Study events recorded at the step. {#tbl-events}")
```

The record of each event names neither the study nor the run in which it occurred. DEV-010-01 names the skid `{python} EV1_EQ`, the first skid, on which the qualification `{python} SDM_ID` and the planned univariate study `{python} UNI_ID` ran. No result of the planned study is in the record, so an event in one of its runs affects no result of this report. The assessments below cover the case in which an event occurred in a run of the qualification.

### DEV-010-01, transmembrane pressure above the NOR {#sec-dev1}

During concentration the TMP of one run rose to `{python} u_("tmp", dev_010_01_tmp_max_psi)`, above the upper edge of its NOR of `{python} u_("tmp", NOR["tmp"][1])`. In-process TMP monitoring detected the excursion. The investigation attributed it to a transient fouling of the membrane, and the run was retained. The excursion lay within the range studied of `{python} rng_s("tmp")`, over which every aggregate result of `{python} UNI2_ID` met its criterion (@sec-criteria). Suppose the run was one of the scale-down runs of `{python} SDM_ID` and was held at that TMP throughout. The upper end of the 95 % confidence interval of the slope of aggregate on TMP then puts its effect at no more than `{python} fx(DEV1_EFFECT_HI, 3)` percentage points. It would have raised the mean of the `{python} w(N_SD)` scale-down runs, and with it the aggregate offset, by at most `{python} fx(DEV1_SHIFT, 3)` percentage points. With the offset lowered by that amount, every aggregate result at manufacturing scale would still meet the criterion.

### DEV-010-02, final concentration below target {#sec-dev2}

The final concentration check of one run measured `{python} u_("final_conc", dev_010_02_conc_pre_g_per_l)` by A280 (`{python} EV2_METHOD`), below the target of `{python} sp_s("final_conc")` and inside the NOR of `{python} nor_s("final_conc")`. The investigation attributed the shortfall to the residual hold-up volume of the skid, the property of the bench skid that @sec-sdm expects to lower its step yield. The record does not say how the hold-up lowered the final concentration. The retentate was concentrated further to the target, which kept it in the pump loop for a further period at the highest concentration of the run. The run was retained. The record gives neither the concentration after the correction nor the run.

The correction could have raised the aggregate of that run. Had the run been one of the scale-down runs of `{python} SDM_ID`, it would enter both the offset of the final concentration and the aggregate offset. The final concentration has no criterion at this step. The aggregate offset of `{python} fx(OFF[AG]["offset"], 3)` percentage points lies between `{python} fx(OFF_DROP_LO, 3)` and `{python} fx(OFF_DROP_HI, 3)` when any one scale-down run is left out. With the smallest of these, the highest aggregate result at manufacturing scale is `{python} fx(AGG_MAX_DROP)` % HMW, `{python} fx(AGG_MARGIN_DROP)` percentage points below the criterion, so no conclusion depends on the run.

## Discrepancies from the plan {#sec-discrepancies}

@tbl-discrepancies lists the `{python} w(N_PD)` discrepancies from PCP-010.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(discrepancy_register(DOC))
print()
print(": Discrepancies from the plan PCP-010. {#tbl-discrepancies}")
```

The first, `{python} PD1`, is work that the plan did not foresee. PCP-010 planned the univariate study `{python} UNI_ID`, which ran but left no result for any parameter effect. The further study `{python} UNI2_ID` was made during the re-analysis to give the parameters recorded results, and every result, PAR and class of this report rests on it (@sec-univariate). It ran on the second skid, with the offsets of the first applied to its results (@sec-sdm). No result for a parameter effect existed when it was made, so no conclusion rests on runs added after a result was known.

`{python} PD[2]` and `{python} PD[7]` concern the buffer exchange. Without the conductivity and pH readings the criterion of PCP-010 could not be judged as planned, and the buffer exchange is controlled by the minimum number of diavolumes and the release of the drug substance (@sec-buffer).

The absence of load, pre-diafiltration and permeate samples (`{python} PD[3]`) leaves the change across the step unknown for aggregate and the acidic charge variants, and the retention of the antibody unconfirmed (@sec-sampling). The missing execution records (`{python} PD[4]`) mean that the randomized order, the single load pool, the method variability, the stability period of the samples and the second-person review of the calculations cannot be shown from the record (@sec-operation, @sec-stats). The incomplete qualification record (`{python} PD[5]`) names no batches and gives no date for the offsets, and the final retentate was compared in place of the change across the step (@sec-sdm).

`{python} PD[6]` covers the rules that PCP-010 leaves to this report. They are the qualification decision without a response-surface model (@sec-sdm), the use of the rule for small changes beside the slope test (@sec-stats), the threshold for a small change and for an attribute that approaches its criterion (@sec-criteria, @sec-par-table), the fit of the buffer exchange across runs and the pure error pooled from every level (@sec-stats).

`{python} PD[8]` is the verification of aggregate at this step, which PCP-010 §7.2 did not plan. PCMP-001 Version 1.0 assumed that no step after cation exchange changes aggregate, and PCMP-001 Version 2.0 §7.5 checks that assumption on `{python} UNI2_ID`. A fit of the main effects of the `{python} w(N_P)` parameters across all runs of the study, evaluated at the least favourable NOR combination, gave a one-sided 95 % prediction bound of a single run of `{python} fx(UF_ALLOW, 3)` percentage points. That bound replaced the assumption of no change and tightened the criterion of the cation exchange pool to `{python} fx(CEX_AG)` % HMW (@sec-basis-par).
